docs.title: Calibrated local classification
clef
docs.text:
Run Cloudflare's clef-flash decision model locally. Give it an input and a set of options, get a calibrated probability for every option in one forward pass. No text generation, no parsing.

Get started HTTP API GitHub

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Classification in one call

    POST /v1/classify with labels returns a probability per label. Multi-label, scoring and saved classifiers included.

    Classification guide

  • OpenAI and Hugging Face compatible

    The official OpenAI SDK (structured outputs) and Hugging Face zero-shot clients work against your own machine.

    Compatibility

  • Evaluation and calibration

    Accuracy, F1, a confusion matrix and calibration for your own labelled data, plus a threshold curve for auto-routing. In the API and in the console.

    Evaluation

  • Async jobs and webhooks

    Submit up to 100,000 rows, poll or get a signed webhook, and stream the results as JSON, NDJSON or CSV.

    Jobs & webhooks

  • Smaller GPUs

    CPU offload and int8 for 16, 12 and 8 GB cards, with measured latency and accuracy.

    Smaller GPUs

  • Safe remote access

    Named API keys, rate limits, CORS and a TLS reverse proxy example.

    Remote access

docs.title: clef v3 - architecture & API contract
docs.text: This file is the contract between the server modules, the backends, the CLI, the web console, the clients and the tests. Change it first, then the code.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
pip install / uv tool install installs two packages from src/ and one console script, clef.

Module Owns clef_server/__init__.py __version__; calls backend.prepare_environment() once (torch-free, before any torch import) clef_server/config.py Config dataclass from CLEF_* env vars, VERSION, MODEL_REPO/MODEL_REVISION, parse_api_keys clef_server/paths.py state dir, log/pid files, classifiers dir, resolve_model_path(cfg) (never downloads) clef_server/dotenv.py optional .env loading: ./.env then ~/.config/clef/env fill os.environ before Config is built (non-empty set variables win, empty counts as unset; only CLEF_* and GEMINI_API_KEY are taken, other names are ignored with a warning naming them; CLEF_ENV_FILE overrides, empty disables, and is read from the real environment once per process, so a file cannot redirect loading); called by config.load(), cli.main and doctor; the server logs the loaded file names (never values) at startup clef_server/backend.py the only place with device-specific code: detection, dtype, sync, OOM, memory, telemetry, preflight, quantization config (bitsandbytes / torchao), device memory cap, pinned host copies (HostCopier) clef_server/offload.py CPU offload: plan_layers (which decoder layers stay on the host) and LayerStreamer (async copy-in per forward); pure logic plus a copier supplied by backend.py clef_server/engine.py background model load (load_model: standard, quantized or offloaded), single GPU worker thread, micro-batching, length bucketing, warmup clef_server/schemas.py pydantic v2 SystemOne request/response models + strict validation clef_server/classify.py classification API models + translation classify/score <-> SystemOne records/answers clef_server/classifiers.py saved-classifier store (ClassifierStore on db.py: versions, owner, audit; one-time import of v3.1 JSON files) clef_server/security.py multi-key auth, per-key rate limiting, CORS setup clef_server/logs.py stdlib-only logging: text / JSON formatters, the request-id context, secret redaction for the access log, uvicorn's log_config clef_server/media.py data-URL / (optional) URL fetching with SSRF guard + caps, image/video decode clef_server/stats.py request log ring buffer, latency histogram, counters, forward stats, time series ring buffer clef_server/appctx.py AppContext: what a feature module gets from create_app() (config, stats, engine, auth / rate-limit dependencies, inference helpers, lifecycle hooks) clef_server/main.py FastAPI app factory create_app(cfg, engine), core routes, middleware, error mapping, FEATURES (feature modules mounted on the context), run(cfg) clef_server/compat.py, compat_openai.py, compat_hf.py, compat_schema.py, compat_errors.py OpenAI (/v1/models, /v1/chat/completions) and Hugging Face zero-shot (/hf/models/{id}) routes; JSON-schema -> questions translation; client-shaped errors clef_server/evaluation.py metric math (compute_metrics), POST /v1/evaluate and /v1/evaluate/metrics, the evaluate job kind clef_server/jobs.py, clef_server/webhooks.py async jobs (database store, the priority / fair-share / off-hours scheduler, /v1/jobs* routes, built-in kinds) and signed, SSRF-guarded webhook delivery clef_server/jobsort.py F2, opt-in: length sort inside a job window and tokenize-ahead for jobs (see Job throughput) clef_server/cli.py the clef command (serve/stop/status/logs/doctor/download/bench/open/version); download is a pinned, resumable snapshot_download with a disk-space check clef_server/doctor.py environment checks per backend, including a recommended memory setting; main(argv) -> int clef_server/httpbench.py the async HTTP load test (clef bench; bench/http_bench.py is a shim) clef_server/static/ Clef Console (zero-build Preact + htm SPA, vendored uPlot; screens in screens/) served at / clef_client/ sync + async Python client (httpx), typed classify results clients/js/ dependency-free ESM JS/TS client (fetch), Node 18+ and browsers clef_server/db.py Database (SQLAlchemy Core engine from CLEF_DATABASE_URL), transactions, Alembic upgrade, jobs.db→clef.db copy, URL redaction, audit() helper clef_server/dbschema.py the SQLAlchemy MetaData and every Table in this document (one place; migrations mirror it) clef_server/migrations/ Alembic env.py, script.py.mako, versions/NNNN_*.py clef_server/models/ base.py (DecisionModel, LocalTensorAdapter, Capabilities, ModelSpec, UnknownModel), registry.py (clef.models entry points, CLEF_MODEL), clef_release.py (clef-flash, clef 27B) clef_server/keystore.py principals, hashed keys, key cache, quotas (Quotas), on db.py; shared by the server and clef keys clef_server/admin.py feature module: /v1/whoami, /v1/admin/keys*, /v1/admin/audit clef_server/schedule.py pure off-hours window maths for the job scheduler (Window, parse_window; DST rules); the Scheduler itself is in jobs.py clef_server/cache.py in-memory LRU result cache used by Engine.prepare / Engine.submit clef_server/router.py, clef_server/review.py, clef_server/llm.py feature module: routers, label-set versions, the Review routes (/v1/routers*, /v1/review*); review.py is the store of the review and llm_calls tables; the OpenAI-compatible LLM client clef_server/batches.py feature module: OpenAI /v1/files* and /v1/batches* on the batch job kind

Invariants (unchanged from v2): - ONE uvicorn worker per process (one model adapter, one model), ONE thread ever touches the GPU (the engine worker). - Python >=3.10 (the WSL venv is 3.10): no typing.Self, tomllib, ExceptionGroup or other 3.11+ features. - Never edit files in the model directory; wrap or re-implement in the engine.

docs.title: Configuration (config.py)
docs.text:
All settings come from env vars. The CLI flags of clef serve set the same env vars.

Env Default Meaning CLEF_MODEL_PATH unset release dir. Unset: ~/models/clef-flash if it holds a release, else the pinned HF cache snapshot CLEF_MODEL_REPO / CLEF_MODEL_REVISION Cloudflare/clef-flash / pinned sha what clef download fetches and the cache lookup uses CLEF_DEVICE auto auto, cuda, rocm, mps, cpu (cuda:1 / rocm:1 select an index) CLEF_DTYPE auto auto, bfloat16, float16, float32 (auto: see backend dtype rules) CLEF_QUANT none none, int8, nf4. int8: bitsandbytes on CUDA, torchao on ROCm / MPS / CPU. nf4: bitsandbytes only (CUDA, and ROCm where it is not recommended); refused elsewhere with a clear error CLEF_QUANT_BACKEND auto auto, bnb, torchao: the library behind CLEF_QUANT (auto: CUDA keeps bitsandbytes, everything else torchao; nf4 is bitsandbytes only) CLEF_OFFLOAD none none or cpu: keep the embeddings and the layers that do not fit under the device budget in host RAM and stream them in per forward (CUDA and ROCm; a warning and no effect on MPS / CPU, which share one memory pool) CLEF_MAX_DEVICE_MEMORY_GB 0 device memory this process may allocate, applied as a hard allocator limit; 0 = no cap (offload then plans from free memory). 2.5 GB of it is reserved for activations when planning the split CLEF_PREFLIGHT 1 memory check before loading CLEF_TELEMETRY 1 GPU telemetry via pynvml / amdsmi / rocm-smi when available CLEF_HOST / CLEF_PORT 127.0.0.1 / 8910 bind address. A non-loopback host without keys logs a loud warning CLEF_API_KEY unset one key, named default CLEF_API_KEYS unset name:key,name2:key2 or a path to a file with one name:key per line (# comments) CLEF_RATE_LIMIT 0 requests per minute per key (per client IP when auth is off); 0 = off CLEF_DRAIN_S 0 seconds main.run keeps serving after the first SIGTERM / Ctrl-C with /readyz 503 draining (see GET /readyz); >= 0, 0 = stop at once. --drain-s CLEF_CORS_ORIGINS empty comma-separated allowed origins (* allowed); empty = CORS off CLEF_STATE_DIR per OS Linux $XDG_STATE_HOME/clef (~/.local/state/clef), macOS ~/Library/Application Support/clef, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\clef. Legacy alias CLEF_LOG_DIR CLEF_MAX_LABELS 64 labels per classify request / saved classifier CLEF_MAX_CLASSIFIERS 1000 saved classifiers CLEF_CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD 0.5 default multi-label threshold (also used by /v1/chat/completions array properties) CLEF_MAX_EVAL_ROWS 500 rows per POST /v1/evaluate request CLEF_MAX_JOB_EVAL_ROWS 100000 rows per evaluate job and per POST /v1/evaluate/metrics request CLEF_MAX_JOB_ITEMS 100000 items per classify / score / systemone job CLEF_MAX_JOBS 100 queued + running jobs (more: 409 with Retry-After) CLEF_JOB_TTL_HOURS 168 finished jobs and their rows are purged this long after they finish; 0 keeps them forever CLEF_JOB_ENGINE_WAIT_S 600 how long a job waits for an unavailable engine before failing CLEF_WEBHOOK_ALLOW empty hosts (hooks.example.com, *.corp.example.net), IPs and CIDRs webhooks may be delivered to; empty = webhooks off CLEF_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_S 10 total timeout of one delivery attempt CLEF_WEBHOOK_ATTEMPTS 10 delivery attempts for final events (job.progress is never retried) CLEF_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_S 2 gauge sampling period for the time series (memory, telemetry, queue) CLEF_INTERACTIVE_BURST 8 interactive micro-batches in a row before waiting background (job) work gets one; >= 1 CLEF_LOG_FORMAT text text or json: server log lines (app, uvicorn, access log); json = one object per line, see Logging CLEF_DATABASE_URL unset SQLAlchemy URL. Unset: sqlite:///<state_dir>/clef.db. postgresql:// / postgres:// are normalised to postgresql+psycopg:// (needs the postgres extra). See Storage CLEF_DATABASE_POOL_SIZE 5 Postgres pool size (max_overflow = the same); ignored on SQLite; >= 1 CLEF_MODEL clef-flash <id>[@<revision>] from the model catalog (clef-flash, clef). CLEF_MODEL_PATH / _REPO / _REVISION stay as aliases, see Decision model interface CLEF_MASK_FREE 0 1: text batches call the backbone with attention_mask=None and the head uses CPU lengths (D2; becomes the default only after bench/parity.py passes) CLEF_FAST_HEAD 0 1: the batch-vectorised, sync-free joint head fast_joint_head (D2; same maths as the release head, opt-in until bench/perf_check.sh passes on the GPU) CLEF_CACHE_SIZE 10000 result-cache entries (in-memory LRU); 0 = off CLEF_CACHE_MB 256 result-cache byte budget (stored-JSON size estimate); 0 = off CLEF_JOB_TZ UTC IANA zone for job windows that give no tz and for CLEF_JOB_WINDOW CLEF_JOB_WINDOW empty default window HH:MM-HH:MM for jobs without schedule; empty = always open CLEF_JOB_ACTIVE 4 jobs that may be running (taking turns) at once; >= 1 CLEF_JOB_AGING_S 3600 a waiting job's class rises one level per this many seconds without a turn (never to urgent); 0 = no aging CLEF_JOB_SORT_WINDOW 0 F2: a job takes N items at a time (N >= 1; 256-1024 recommended), sorts the ones that need a forward by token length and sends them in micro-batches; results are persisted per window in input order. 0 = off. Default flips only if bench/sort_check.sh shows a gain over 10% on the GPU CLEF_TOKENIZE_AHEAD 0 F2: 1: the next window (a micro-batch when the sort is off) is encoded on CPU threads (ctx.prepare) while the current one is on the GPU. Same flip rule as the sort GEMINI_API_KEY unset the router's LLM key. Unset (and no CLEF_LLM_API_KEY) = router LLM off. Never logged; clef doctor only says whether it is set CLEF_LLM_API_KEY unset key for another OpenAI-compatible provider; wins over GEMINI_API_KEY CLEF_LLM_BASE_URL https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/ OpenAI-compatible endpoint (ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenAI work the same) CLEF_LLM_MODEL gemini-3.8-flash model id sent to the endpoint CLEF_LLM_TIMEOUT_S 60 total timeout of one LLM call (2 retries on 429 / 5xx) CLEF_ROUTER_BATCH 20 buffered items per proposal call CLEF_ROUTER_COLD_BATCH 20 buffered items before the cold-start (bootstrap) call CLEF_ROUTER_FLUSH_S 600 flush a non-empty buffer after this long even if it is below the batch size CLEF_ROUTER_MODE review default mode of new routers: review or auto CLEF_ROUTER_MAX_NEW_PER_DAY 10 auto mode: labels a router may add per UTC day CLEF_ROUTER_MAX_INPUT_CHARS 500 each buffered input is truncated to this before it is sent to the LLM CLEF_REVIEW_TTL_DAYS 30 review items' input text is deleted this long after creation (and at once when resolved) CLEF_MAX_FILE_MB 200 body limit for POST /v1/files only (everything else keeps CLEF_MAX_BODY_MB) CLEF_MAX_BATCH_LINES 50000 lines per batch input file; the effective cap is min(this, CLEF_MAX_JOB_ITEMS) CLEF_FILE_TTL_HOURS 720 uploaded files without expires_after are purged this long after upload v2 knobs unchanged CLEF_MAX_TOKENS, CLEF_MAX_BODY_MB, CLEF_MAX_IMAGES/VIDEOS/PIXELS/FRAMES, CLEF_VIDEO_FPS, CLEF_MAX_BATCH, CLEF_MAX_QUESTIONS, CLEF_ALLOW_URL_FETCH, CLEF_URL_FETCH_MAX_MB, CLEF_MAX_MICROBATCH, CLEF_BATCH_WINDOW_MS, CLEF_BUCKETS, CLEF_PAD_MULTIPLE (64, measured on ROCm only), CLEF_PAD_TO_BUCKET, CLEF_WARMUP, CLEF_TUNABLEOP_ONLINE (0: live forwards never tune; idle background tuning), CLEF_TUNABLEOP_IDLE_S (2: quiet seconds before a tune step), CLEF_LOG_STATE, CLEF_LOG_BUFFER

Config validates enums (device, dtype, quant, quant backend, offload, log format), CLEF_MAX_DEVICE_MEMORY_GB >= 0, the threshold range, CLEF_RATE_LIMIT >= 0, CLEF_INTERACTIVE_BURST >= 1 and CLEF_DRAIN_S >= 0 in __post_init__ (ValueError on a bad value) and exposes api_keys() -> dict[name, key], auth_required, is_loopback, public_limits().

docs.title: Backend interface (backend.py)
docs.text:
class BackendError(RuntimeError): ...       # unavailable explicit device, unsupported quant/dtype combination
class PreflightError(RuntimeError): ...     # not enough free memory for the chosen dtype/quant (clear message)

def prepare_environment(environ: MutableMapping[str, str] = os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Torch-free. setdefault() the per-platform env BEFORE torch is imported. Returns the names it set.
    - torch build is ROCm (importlib.metadata version of torch contains "+rocm"):
        TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL=1, and on WSL (/dev/dxg exists) HSA_ENABLE_DXG_DETECTION=1;
        PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_* unless CLEF_TUNABLEOP=0 (on by default). HSA_* / AOTriton are NEVER set on other backends.
    - macOS: PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1.
    - everywhere: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is NOT set here (the CLI download needs the network; the engine passes
      local paths so it never downloads)."""

def detect(requested: str = "auto") -> Backend:
    """auto: cuda (NVIDIA: torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.version.hip is None) > rocm (torch.version.hip)
    > mps (torch.backends.mps.is_available()) > cpu. An explicit request that is unavailable raises BackendError
    with a hint (wrong torch build, driver missing, HSA_ENABLE_DXG_DETECTION on WSL, ...)."""

@dataclass
class Backend:
    name: str                     # "cuda" | "rocm" | "mps" | "cpu"
    device: torch.device          # cuda:N for cuda AND rocm, mps, cpu
    def synchronize(self) -> None
    def empty_cache(self) -> None
    def is_oom(self, exc: BaseException) -> bool       # torch.OutOfMemoryError / cuda OOM / MPS "out of memory"
    def device_name(self) -> str                       # "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090", "Apple M3 Max", CPU brand
    def memory(self) -> dict                           # see below; never raises
    def telemetry(self) -> dict                        # see below; never raises, "unavailable" elsewhere
    def resolve_dtype(self, requested: str) -> tuple[torch.dtype, str | None]   # (dtype, warning or None)
    def versions(self) -> dict                         # {"torch","cuda","hip","driver","macos"} (None if n/a)
    def fast_path(self) -> dict                        # {"causal_conv1d": bool, "fla": bool, "expected": bool}

def preflight(backend: Backend, dtype: torch.dtype, quant: str, weights_gb: float,
              cap_gb: float = 0.0, offload: str = "none") -> list[str]:
    """Raise PreflightError when free memory (or the CLEF_MAX_DEVICE_MEMORY_GB cap) is clearly below what the load
    needs; return warnings when close. With offload=cpu on cuda / rocm the engine plans the split itself and only
    the cap is checked here."""

def quant_method(backend: Backend, quant: str, choice: str = "auto") -> str:
    """"bnb" or "torchao". auto: nf4 -> bnb; int8 -> bnb on cuda, torchao on rocm / mps / cpu.
    An explicit choice wins (nf4 + torchao is a BackendError)."""

def quantization_config(backend: Backend, quant: str, dtype: torch.dtype, choice: str = "auto") -> Any | None:
    """None for "none". Else a transformers config: BitsAndBytesConfig (int8 / nf4; cuda and rocm only) or
    TorchAoConfig(Int8WeightOnlyConfig) with the embeddings and the vision tower left in bf16. BackendError with
    an install hint when the library is missing or the backend cannot run it."""

def recommend_memory_setting(backend: Backend, weights_gb: float = 19.0) -> str | None:
    """One line of advice from the detected memory (printed by `clef doctor`); None when bf16 fits."""

Offload support on Backend: has_discrete_memory (true on cuda / rocm), pin_host(tensor), host_copier() (a HostCopier that copies pinned host tensors on a side stream) and apply_memory_cap(cap_gb) (torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction; returns whether a limit was set). ACTIVATION_RESERVE_GB = 2.5.

Dtype rules (resolve_dtype("auto")): bf16 on cuda (if torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(), else fp16 + warning), rocm, and mps on macOS >= 14 (fp16 + warning before 14); cpu: bf16 when the CPU supports it, else fp32. An explicit dtype the device cannot run falls back the same way with a warning. Any fallback must be validated for probability parity against bf16 (bench/parity.py, results in docs/hardware-results.md).

memory(): {"kind": "vram"|"unified"|"system", "total_gb", "allocated_gb", "reserved_gb", "free_gb"} (floats or None). cuda/rocm: torch.cuda.mem_get_info/memory_allocated/memory_reserved; mps: torch.mps.current_allocated_memory, driver_allocated_memory, recommended_max_memory; cpu: process RSS and system memory (psutil if installed, else None).

telemetry(): {"available": bool, "source": "nvml"|"amdsmi"|"rocm-smi"|None, "util_pct", "temp_c", "power_w", "mem_used_gb", "mem_total_gb"}; values None when unknown. Imports pynvml / amdsmi lazily; failures are logged once at debug level and turn the result into {"available": false, ...}. rocm-smi (subprocess) results are cached for >= 2 s. Under WSL (measured, 7900 XTX) amdsmi gives utilization + temperature only; its VRAM usage is impossible (> total) and is dropped.

docs.title: Engine interface (engine.py)
docs.text:
Record = dict  # sanitized: {"model": str, "state": Any, "questions": dict,
               #             "images": list[PIL.Image.Image] | None, "videos": list[np.ndarray] | None}

class EngineNotReady(RuntimeError): ...          # -> HTTP 503
class InputTooLarge(ValueError): ...             # -> HTTP 413 (e.g. schema alone exceeds max_tokens)
class GpuOutOfMemory(RuntimeError): ...          # -> HTTP 503 (after backend.empty_cache())

class Engine:
    def __init__(self, cfg: Config, stats: Stats, loader: Callable | None = None,
                 backend: Backend | None = None): ...
        # loader: test injection; default resolves the model dir (paths.resolve_model_path) and imports
        #   joint_schema_model from it. backend: test injection; default backend.detect(cfg.device),
        #   done on the worker thread at load time (so a BackendError becomes status "error", not a crash).
    status: str             # "loading" | "warming" | "ready" | "error"
    error: str | None
    load_seconds: float | None
    def start(self) -> None
    async def decide(self, records: list[Record], priority: str = "interactive") -> list[Result]
        # results in input order; priority is "interactive" (default) or "background" (ValueError otherwise)
    def info(self) -> dict
    def sample(self) -> dict    # cheap gauges for the time series, see below; never raises; any thread
    def shutdown(self) -> None

info() (also the bulk of /health): 

{"backend": "rocm", "device": "cuda:0", "dtype": "bfloat16", "quant": "none",
 "model_path": "/home/<user>/models/clef-flash", "torch": "2.11.0+rocm7.2", "transformers": "5.10.2",
 "gpu": {"available": true, "name": "AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX", "memory_kind": "vram", "vram_total_gb": 23.94,
         "vram_allocated_gb": 17.79, "vram_reserved_gb": 18.17, "vram_free_gb": 5.4},
 "telemetry": {"available": false, "source": null, "util_pct": null, "temp_c": null, "power_w": null,
               "mem_used_gb": null, "mem_total_gb": null},
 "fast_path": {"causal_conv1d": false, "fla": true, "expected": true},
 "versions": {"torch": "2.11.0+rocm7.2", "cuda": null, "hip": "7.2", "driver": null, "macos": null},
 "warnings": []}
Before the backend is detected (status == "loading" early) backend is null and the gpu block has available: false. gpu keeps the v2 key names for compatibility; on mps memory_kind is "unified" and vram_total_gb is recommended_max_memory; on cpu available is false. info() must stay fast (< 5 ms): it returns the cached telemetry from the last sample().

sample() -> {"mem_used_gb": float|None, "mem_total_gb": float|None, "gpu_util_pct": float|None, "gpu_temp_c": float|None, "gpu_power_w": float|None} (memory = allocated on cuda/rocm/mps, RSS on cpu).

Rules (v2 rules kept): - Exactly ONE thread ever runs forwards (the worker). decide() enqueues and awaits futures. - Text-only records are coalesced for up to batch_window_ms / max_microbatch, grouped by length bucket, one forward per group, right-padded to the next pad_multiple. Media records run alone, unpadded. - Two priority lanes: interactive (everything through ctx.infer, and direct engine.decide() calls) and background (ctx.decide: jobs, the evaluate job kind). Each lane is FIFO. The worker waits for the first item of either lane, lets the batch window run, and only then picks the lane for the micro-batch, so an interactive item that arrives during a window opened by background work still goes first. A micro-batch holds ONE class: interactive whenever any is queued (up to the starvation bound below), else background. Micro-batching and bucketing work as before inside it. - Classes are not mixed even when the micro-batch has room. The model is compute-bound (batching adds ~30% throughput), so an interactive record riding in a batch of 8 background records pays nearly the whole batch's forward time; running it alone first costs the job one extra host overhead (~50% of a single forward). - Starvation bound: after CLEF_INTERACTIVE_BURST (default 8) interactive micro-batches in a row while background work was waiting, the next micro-batch is background. A steady interactive load therefore leaves jobs at least 1 of every N+1 micro-batches. A micro-batch already taken is never preempted: all of its groups (one forward per length bucket, one per media record) run before the worker looks at the lanes again. - Warmup: one forward per bucket (<= 1024) at batch sizes {1, max_microbatch}; status "warming" meanwhile. - No torch.cuda.* outside backend.py. OOM: backend.is_oom(exc) -> backend.empty_cache() -> GpuOutOfMemory; the worker keeps running. Timing uses backend.synchronize(). - Load order on the worker: detect backend -> resolve dtype -> resolve model path -> preflight (if enabled) -> load_model(...): apply the device cap (CLEF_MAX_DEVICE_MEMORY_GB), build the quantization config, then either the standard path (load_release_model(path, device=..., dtype=..., quantization_config=...), kwarg only when quantizing) or, with CLEF_OFFLOAD=cpu on cuda / rocm, an offloaded load. Each failure becomes status "error" with a one-line actionable message. - Offloaded load (offload.py): token and output embeddings (~4 GB) stay on the host and are gathered on the CPU; decoder layers beyond the device budget (cap or free memory, minus ACTIVATION_RESERVE_GB) are held in pinned host memory, spread evenly through the stack, and copied in on a side stream one or two layers ahead of the compute; the vision tower, final norm, rotary tables and the joint head stay on the device. The weights are the same tensors, so probabilities are identical to a normal run. After a failed forward the streamer puts the layers back on the host. Measured numbers: memory.md. - The engine reports stats.record_forward(...) and stats.set_queue_depth(n, by_class={"interactive": i, "background": b}) (n = i + b, the v2 total).

docs.title: Stats interface (stats.py)
docs.text:
class Stats:
    def __init__(self, buffer: int = 1000, retention_s: int = 3600): ...
    def record_request(self, entry: dict) -> None   # entry = /v1/log item minus id/ts; may include "key"
    def record_forward(self, n_records: int, n_tokens: int, padded_tokens: int, ms: float) -> None
    def set_queue_depth(self, n: int, by_class: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> None
                                                    # n = total; by_class -> /v1/stats queue_depth_by_class
    def sample(self, gauges: dict) -> None          # engine.sample() + {"queue_depth"}; called every
                                                    # cfg.sample_interval_s by main; unknown keys ignored
    def in_flight(self) -> ContextManager
    def snapshot(self, window_s: int = 300) -> dict   # the /v1/stats body (minus status/gpu, added by main)
    def timeseries(self, window_s: int = 300, step_s: int | None = None) -> dict
    def latest_point(self, step_s: int = 5) -> dict   # the newest (current, partial) step as one point
    def log(self, limit: int = 100, since: int | None = None) -> list[dict]
    async def subscribe(self) -> AsyncIterator[dict]

Internally the time series is a ring of 1-second buckets covering retention_s (3600). Each bucket holds: request count, error count, successful latencies (capped at 1000 per second), forward count/records/tokens/padded, max queue depth seen (from set_queue_depth and sample), and the last gauge sample. Thread-safe (engine thread + event loop + sampler).

docs.title: Feature modules (appctx.py)
docs.text:
New API surface is added as a feature module instead of growing main.py. A module exposes router(ctx: AppContext) -> APIRouter and is listed in main.FEATURES (currently ["evaluation", "compat", "jobs"], in that order: evaluation registers its job kind before jobs reads the registry). create_app() builds the context, imports each module with importlib and includes its router.

AppContext fields:

Field What it is cfg, stats, engine, store the Config, Stats, Engine and ClassifierStore of this app auth, limited FastAPI dependency lists: auth goes on every router that needs a key, limited adds the rate limit on inference routes errors the shared OpenAPI responses for the standard error statuses infer(request, reqs, batch, label="batch") the request path: limits, media load, one engine.decide(priority="interactive"), and the request log / stats entry decide(reqs, batch=True, label="batch", priority="background") the same without a request, for background work (jobs, the evaluate kind): limits, media and one engine.decide() in the background lane; not logged or counted in stats map_exception(exc), api_error(status, detail, headers=None), request_id(request) the shared error mapping (raise the result from exc) run_classify, run_classify_batch, run_score the classification routes' implementations, reusable by other features on_startup, on_shutdown lists of async callables run inside the app lifespan after the engine starts / before it stops (jobs start and stop their runner here) extra a dict features use to publish objects to each other; extra["job_kinds"] is the job-kind registry

Rules for a feature: inference goes through ctx.infer or ctx.decide (never straight to the engine), routes carry ctx.auth (and ctx.limited when they run the model), and all request / response models are pydantic so the route appears in openapi.json.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text: Route Purpose Section GET /health, GET /livez, GET /readyz, GET /schema-example status, liveness, readiness, copy-paste bodies (open) below POST /v1/systemone, POST /v1/batch the original typed questions API below POST /v1/classify, /v1/classify/batch, /v1/score; PUT|GET|DELETE /v1/classifiers/{name}, GET /v1/classifiers, POST /v1/classifiers/{name}[/batch] classification below GET /v1/models[/{id}], POST /v1/chat/completions OpenAI-compatible structured outputs Compat POST /hf/models/{id} (and the hidden POST /models/{id}) Hugging Face zero-shot classification Compat POST /v1/evaluate, POST /v1/evaluate/metrics accuracy, F1, confusion matrix, calibration Evaluation POST /v1/jobs, GET /v1/jobs, GET /v1/jobs/{id}, GET /v1/jobs/{id}/results, POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel, DELETE /v1/jobs/{id} async jobs Jobs GET /v1/stats, /v1/stats/timeseries, /v1/log, /v1/events observability (console) below GET /v1/classifiers/{name}/versions[/{v}] classifier history Storage GET /v1/whoami, /v1/admin/keys*, GET /v1/admin/audit principals, keys, quotas, audit Keys and principals /v1/routers*, /v1/review* self-evolving router, human review queue Review queue and router /v1/files*, /v1/batches* OpenAI Files + Batch API OpenAI Files and Batches

docs.title: Auth, rate limit, CORS (security.py)
docs.text:
• Keys: CLEF_API_KEY and/or CLEF_API_KEYS (see Configuration; every env key is a full admin, and startup warns when there is more than one). When any key exists every /v1/* route, and the Hugging Face routes (/hf/models/*, /models/*), need X-API-Key: <key> or Authorization: Bearer <key> (401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer otherwise; the OpenAI and HF routes render that in their own error shape). For SSE /v1/events?key=<key> is also accepted for plain EventSource clients, which cannot set headers (the console sends the header; see Logging for how the query value is masked). Comparison is constant-time over all keys. The matching key's name (never the key) is stored on request.state.key_name and written to the request log ("key") and to /v1/stats (by_key). Auth off -> key is null.
  • Open routes: /, static files, /health, /livez, /readyz, /schema-example, /docs, /openapi.json.
  • Rate limit (CLEF_RATE_LIMIT=N): sliding 60 s window per key name (per client IP when auth is off), counted on the POST inference routes only (/v1/systemone, /v1/batch, /v1/classify, /v1/classify/batch, /v1/score, POST /v1/classifiers/{name}[/batch], /v1/chat/completions, /hf/models/*, /v1/evaluate, POST /v1/jobs). /v1/evaluate/metrics and the job read / cancel / delete routes are not counted. Over the limit: 429 {"detail": "rate limit exceeded (N/min)", "request_id"} + Retry-After: <int seconds>. Rejected requests are logged (status 429) but not counted.
  • CORS: off by default. CLEF_CORS_ORIGINS=https://a.example,https://b.example (or *) installs Starlette's CORSMiddleware with methods GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS, headers * (X-API-Key, Authorization, Content-Type), exposed headers X-Request-ID, Retry-After; allow_credentials false.
  • Binding a non-loopback CLEF_HOST without any key logs a multi-line WARNING at startup (main.run).

Body limit: Content-Length (or streamed bytes) > max_body_mb -> 413.

docs.title: POST /v1/systemone, POST /v1/batch
docs.text:
Unchanged from v2 (request, response, validation, error paths). See git history of this file for the full text; summary: 

{"model": "clef-flash", "state": "<string or any JSON>",
 "questions": {"<id>": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "optional", "criteria": {"opt": "desc"}},
               "<id>": {"type": "score", "instructions": "optional", "criteria": ["level0", "level1"]},
               "<id>": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "optional", "criteria": {"true": "desc", "false": "desc"}}},
 "images": ["data:image/...;base64,..."], "videos": ["data:video/mp4;base64,..."]}
-> {"model", "answers": {"<id>": <systemone_answer>}, "usage": {"input_tokens", "output_tokens": 0}, "timing": {"queue_ms", "forward_ms", "total_ms", "batch_size"}}. Answers: choice {"type","choice","confidence","probabilities": {opt: p}}; score {"type","score","confidence","legend": {"0": level0, ...},"probabilities": {"0": p, ...}}; noul {"type","noul": p_true}. /v1/batch: {"batch": [...]} -> {"batch_ms", "results": [...]}, errors name the index (batch[3].questions...).

docs.title: Classification API (classify.py, classifiers.py)
docs.text:
The classification routes are a thin, stable layer over the SAME engine: each input is translated into exactly one SystemOne record (the same record /v1/systemone would build), so probabilities are identical to the equivalent SystemOne call (verified live within 1e-3). All of them are POST inference routes (logged, rate limited, counted in stats) and return usage, timing and request_id like the existing routes.

Labels: either a list of unique non-empty strings (["billing", "technical"]) or an object label -> description ({"billing": "Payments or invoices"}); 2..max_labels labels for single-label, 1..max_labels for multi-label.

Translation (normative - the live parity test rebuilds these exact records): - single-label -> questions = {"label": {"type": "choice", "criteria": C, "instructions": I}} where C = {l: l for l in labels} for a list, the object as given for a dict, and "instructions" is present only when the request has instructions. - multi-label -> one noul question per label, question id = the label: {"type": "noul", "instructions": P + 'Does the label "<label>" apply?'} where P = instructions + " " when given, else ""; plus "criteria": {"true": desc} when labels is a dict and desc != label. - score -> questions = {"score": {"type": "score", "criteria": levels, "instructions": I}} (instructions only when given). - state = input verbatim (string or any JSON); images/videos pass through load_media exactly as on /v1/systemone; model is optional (omitted or null = the served model; another id is 404).

docs.title: POST /v1/classify
docs.text:
{"input": "Checkout is down", "labels": ["billing", "technical"], "instructions": "optional question",
 "multi_label": false, "threshold": 0.5, "images": [], "videos": [], "model": "clef-flash"}
Single-label response: 
{"model": "clef-flash", "multi_label": false, "label": "technical", "confidence": 0.96,
 "scores": {"billing": 0.04, "technical": 0.96},
 "usage": {"input_tokens": 120, "output_tokens": 0},
 "timing": {"queue_ms": 0.4, "forward_ms": 141.2, "total_ms": 150.3, "batch_size": 1}, "request_id": "<hex>"}
(label = the choice answer, confidence = its probability, scores = all options' probabilities.) Multi-label response: "multi_label": true, "labels": [...] = every label with score >= threshold, sorted by score desc (may be empty), "scores": {label: P(true)}, "threshold": 0.5; no label/confidence. threshold is allowed only with multi_label: true (default CLEF_CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD), within [0, 1].

docs.title: POST /v1/classify/batch
docs.text: {"inputs": [<any>, ...] (1..max_batch), "labels": ..., "instructions", "multi_label", "threshold", "model"} (no media in batch). Runs through the engine's micro-batching in one decide() call -> {"batch_ms": float, "results": [<classify response minus request_id>, ...], "request_id": "<hex>"} in input order. Errors name the index: inputs[3]: ....

docs.title: POST /v1/score
docs.text:
{"input": ..., "levels": ["low", "medium", "high"], "instructions": "optional", "images", "videos", "model"} (2..max_labels unique non-empty levels) -> 

{"model": "clef-flash", "score": 1.78, "level": "high", "level_index": 2, "confidence": 0.86,
 "distribution": {"low": 0.07, "medium": 0.07, "high": 0.86}, "usage": {}, "timing": {}, "request_id": "<hex>"}
(score = expected level index, level/level_index = most likely level, distribution keyed by level text.)

docs.title: Saved classifiers
docs.text:
• PUT /v1/classifiers/{name} body {"kind": "classify" | "score", "labels": ... (classify), "levels": [...] (score), "instructions": str?, "multi_label": false, "threshold": float?, "description": str?} -> 200 the stored definition + {"name", "created_at", "updated_at", "version", "owner", "model"} (ISO-8601 UTC; created_at = version 1). A changed definition adds a version, an identical one is a no-op (Storage). Validation as above.
  • GET /v1/classifiers -> {"classifiers": [<definition>, ...]} sorted by name.
  • GET /v1/classifiers/{name} -> the definition, 404 if missing.
  • DELETE /v1/classifiers/{name} -> {"deleted": "<name>"}, 404 if missing.
  • POST /v1/classifiers/{name} {"input": ..., "images"?, "videos"?, "threshold"?} -> the classify (or score) response + "classifier": "<name>".
  • POST /v1/classifiers/{name}/batch {"inputs": [...]} -> the batch response + "classifier".
  • Names: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ (400 otherwise). Stored in the database (classifiers + classifier_versions, see Storage), at most max_classifiers names (409 beyond).

docs.title: OpenAI and Hugging Face compat (compat*.py)
docs.text:
Guide: openai-compat.md. Both dialects translate to ONE SystemOne record per request and go through ctx.infer, so keys, rate limit, log, stats and limits are shared and the probabilities equal the equivalent /v1/systemone call.

  • GET /v1/models lists the served model; GET /v1/models/{id} returns it, any other id is 404 model_not_found (details in Decision model interface).
  • POST /v1/chat/completions: the schema comes from response_format (json_schema) or from exactly one forced tool. Each top-level property becomes one question (compat_schema.py): string enum -> choice; boolean -> noul (true when P >= 0.5); integer enum, bounded integer (2..64 values) or string enum with x-clef-ordinal -> score; array of string enums -> one noul per option (options with P >= CLEF_CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD). Anything else (free text, numbers, nested objects) is a 400 whose param names the property. messages become the state (a lone user message verbatim, otherwise a readable transcript); image_url / video_url parts become images / videos.
  • Response: OpenAI chat.completion with the argmax as JSON in message.content (or a tool_calls entry), logprobs carrying log p (top_logprobs 0..64, floor -9999), usage (completion_tokens always 0) and a non-standard top-level clef object with every probability, timing and request_id. stream: true returns valid SSE (role chunk, one content chunk, finish chunk, optional usage chunk, [DONE]). n > 1, text / json_object response formats and requests without a schema are 400s (missing_schema when no schema was given).
  • POST /hf/models/{model_id:path}: Inference API zero-shot body {inputs, parameters: {candidate_labels, multi_label, hypothesis_template}}. Response {sequence, labels, scores} sorted by score, or [{label, score}] when the User-Agent is hf_hub/1.x (force with ?format=classic|list); inputs may be a list (one micro-batched pass).
  • Errors on these routes use the client's shape (compat_errors.py): OpenAI {"error": {message, type, param, code}}, Hugging Face {"error": "message"}; status codes match the rest of the API.

docs.title: Evaluation (evaluation.py)
docs.text:
Guide: evaluation.md. compute_metrics is the single implementation of the metric math; the console and the job kind use it too.

  • POST /v1/evaluate {labels | classifier, instructions?, multi_label?, threshold?, bins?, rows: [{input, gold}], include_predictions?}: at most CLEF_MAX_EVAL_ROWS rows (400 beyond, pointing at the job kind), classified CLEF_MAX_BATCH at a time through ctx.infer, then scored. A gold label outside the label set is a 400 naming the row, before any inference.
  • POST /v1/evaluate/metrics {labels, rows: [{gold, scores}], multi_label?, threshold?, bins?, include_predictions?}: no inference, at most CLEF_MAX_JOB_EVAL_ROWS rows, not rate limited.
  • Response: n, accuracy, top2_accuracy, macro_f1, micro_f1, weighted_f1, per_label, confusion_matrix {labels, matrix}, calibration {bins, ece, mce, brier, nll, mean_confidence}, coverage_curve, auto_route, optional predictions. Multi-label: exact_match, hamming_loss, per-label tp fp fn tn.
  • evaluate job kind (registered in ctx.extra["job_kinds"]): same payload as POST /v1/evaluate, up to CLEF_MAX_JOB_EVAL_ROWS rows, one stored item per row, result = the metrics object. Not resumable (it restarts).

docs.title: Async jobs and webhooks (jobs.py, webhooks.py)
docs.text:
Guide: jobs.md.

  • POST /v1/jobs {kind, payload, webhook?, metadata?} -> 202 with the job and Location: /v1/jobs/{id}. The payload is fully validated at submit (400 with a path); an unknown kind lists the available ones. Kinds: classify, score, systemone (jobs.py) and evaluate (evaluation.py). 409 + Retry-After when CLEF_MAX_JOBS is reached.
  • GET /v1/jobs?status&kind&limit&offset (newest first), GET /v1/jobs/{id} (status, progress, ETA, result summary, webhook delivery status), GET /v1/jobs/{id}/results (JSON pages with next_offset, or a full stream with ?format=ndjson|csv; CSV neutralises cells starting with =, +, -, @), POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel, DELETE /v1/jobs/{id} (409 while queued or running).
  • Storage: the database (ctx.db: SQLite <state_dir>/clef.db or CLEF_DATABASE_URL; jobs, payloads, result rows, webhook deliveries; see Storage). Statuses: queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled, interrupted. Jobs are scheduled by class and fair share (see Job scheduler), at most CLEF_JOB_ACTIVE at a time, and ONE micro-batch in flight across all of them (CLEF_MAX_MICROBATCH records through ctx.decide), so interactive requests interleave. A job interrupted by a stop or crash resumes after its last stored row on the next start. Rows are appended in one transaction that reads done inside it, so an in-flight chunk is either stored whole or recomputed (no gap, no duplicate). A clean stop (lifespan shutdown) parks the running job as interrupted without counting it; only a job found still running at startup (a crash) increments resumes, and more than CLEF_JOB_MAX_RESUMES crashes fail it. A job whose cancel was requested before the stop or crash ends cancelled at that point (or at the next start), never resumed. Cancel is atomic per state: JobStore.cancel_queued (queued / interrupted -> cancelled), else JobStore.flag_cancel in one transaction (running -> cancel_requested=1; interrupted, i.e. parked meanwhile by a stop or runner error -> cancelled at once), so a park racing the cancel cannot drop it. Every terminal transition (finish, cancel while queued or interrupted, cancel / give-up at recovery) writes the status and the pending terminal webhook record in ONE SQLite transaction, so a crash cannot lose the event. A row the engine rejects becomes an {"index", "error"} row; the job fails only on systemic errors (engine down for CLEF_JOB_ENGINE_WAIT_S). Finished jobs are purged CLEF_JOB_TTL_HOURS after they finish.
  • Ownership: with auth on, a job belongs to the key name that submitted it. Another non-admin principal gets 404 (not in its list either); a key without the jobs scope gets 403; admins see every job, owner-less ones (created while auth was off) included.
  • Webhooks: events job.succeeded, job.failed, job.cancelled (default) and opt-in job.progress (at most one per 10 s, one attempt). Headers X-Clef-Event, X-Clef-Delivery, and with a secret X-Clef-Timestamp and X-Clef-Signature: sha256= HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>". 2xx = delivered; 408 / 425 / 429 / 5xx and network errors retry with exponential backoff up to CLEF_WEBHOOK_ATTEMPTS; other statuses and all redirects are final. A delivery still pending at restart is retried with the same delivery id, but its attempt count and backoff start over (known behaviour). Disabled until CLEF_WEBHOOK_ALLOW is set; the allow-list is checked at submit and on every attempt, the host is resolved then and the connection is pinned to the checked IP (see SECURITY.md).
  • Jobs are not counted in /v1/stats or the request log (they use ctx.decide).
  • Custom kinds: ctx.extra.setdefault("job_kinds", {})[name] = {"validate": fn, "run": async_fn, "resumable": bool} (see jobs.md).

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text: 200 when status is ready or warming, 503 otherwise. {"ready", "status", "version": "3.1.0", **engine.info(), "load_seconds", "uptime_s", "error", "limits": Config.public_limits()}. GET /livez -> 200 {"ok": true}.

docs.title: GET /readyz
docs.text: Readiness for load balancers and orchestrators (open, like /livez). 200 {"ready": true} only when the engine status is ready and the app is not draining; otherwise 503 {"ready": false, "status": "loading|warming|error|draining", "error": <engine error or null>}. Unlike /health, warming is not ready. Draining: uvicorn closes its listening sockets and drains connections BEFORE the lifespan shutdown runs, so a flag set there is never seen by a client. main.run therefore serves through DrainingServer (a uvicorn.Server subclass): the FIRST SIGTERM / Ctrl-C sets app.state.draining = True and keeps serving for CLEF_DRAIN_S seconds (/readyz answers 503 draining, every other route works as usual), then calls uvicorn's own handle_exit and the normal shutdown starts. A second signal during the drain skips the rest of it; after that uvicorn's semantics apply (another Ctrl-C forces the exit). CLEF_DRAIN_S=0 (default) stops at once, as before. The lifespan still sets draining = True first thing at shutdown, for launchers other than main.run (plain uvicorn). A drain only helps a load balancer that probes /readyz faster than it lasts: probe interval x failure threshold must be below CLEF_DRAIN_S, and CLEF_DRAIN_S below the supervisor's stop timeout (Docker sends SIGKILL after 10 s by default; clef stop waits 30 s). Liveness stays on /livez (process up); the Docker HEALTHCHECK uses /readyz with a long start period so a container whose model failed to load turns unhealthy.

docs.title: GET /v1/stats?window_s=300
docs.text: v2 body plus "by_key": {"<name>|anonymous": count} and "by_endpoint": {"/v1/classify": count, ...} over the window, "queue_depth_by_class": {"interactive": n, "background": n} next to the v2 total queue_depth, plus "status" and "gpu" (vram_allocated_gb, vram_reserved_gb, vram_total_gb, memory_kind) and "telemetry" (cached engine telemetry) added by main.

docs.title: GET /v1/stats/timeseries?window_s=300&step_s=5
docs.text:
window_s in 10..3600 (console uses 300 / 900 / 3600); step_s optional, default max(1, window_s // 60) (5 / 15 / 60 s), must satisfy 1 <= step_s <= window_s and window_s / step_s <= 720 (400 otherwise). Columnar (uPlot-friendly), oldest first, n = ceil(window_s / step_s) points aligned to multiples of step_s; the last point is the current, partial step: 

{"window_s": 300, "step_s": 5, "now": 1759480000.2,
 "t":             [1759479705, ...],      // step start, unix seconds
 "rps":           [0.8, ...],             // requests completed in the step / step_s (0 when none)
 "p50_ms":        [141.0, null, ...],     // successful requests completed in the step; null when none
 "p95_ms":        [150.2, null, ...],
 "error_rate":    [0.0, null, ...],       // errors / requests; null when no requests
 "avg_batch":     [1.6, null, ...],       // records / forwards; null when no forwards
 "queue_depth":   [0, ...],               // max seen in the step; null before the first sample
 "padding_ratio": [0.12, null, ...],      // 1 - tokens / padded tokens over the step's forwards; null when none
 "mem_used_gb":   [17.8, ...],            // last gauge sample in the step, else null
 "gpu_util_pct":  [null, ...], "gpu_temp_c": [null, ...], "gpu_power_w": [null, ...]}

docs.title: GET /v1/log?limit=100&since=<id>
docs.text: v2 entries plus "key": "<name>" | null. Endpoint values include the new POST routes (actual path, e.g. /v1/classifiers/support-triage).

docs.title: GET /v1/events?step_s=5 (SSE)
docs.text: event: log + data: <log entry> per request; event: stats + data: <stats body> every 2 s. The stats body carries "point": stats.latest_point(step_s) (same fields as one time-series column entry, scalars, plus t and step_s), so charts append (new t) or replace (same t) their last point without polling. step_s in 1..60, default 5. Auth: the X-API-Key / Bearer header like every route, or ?key= (kept for EventSource clients; masked in the access log).

docs.title: Logging (logs.py)
docs.text:
• setup_logging(fmt) installs one root handler (idempotent; a later call only swaps its formatter). run(cfg) passes uvicorn_log_config(fmt) to uvicorn.run(log_config=...), so the foreground clef serve and the --detach child (python -m clef_server.main) log the same way.
  • CLEF_LOG_FORMAT=text (default): the app keeps "%(asctime)s %(levelname)-7s %(name)s %(message)s", uvicorn keeps its own formatters. json: the app, uvicorn / uvicorn.error and uvicorn.access all write one JSON object per line: {"ts": "<ISO 8601 UTC, ms>", "level", "logger", "msg"} plus "request_id" when the record is emitted inside a request (a ContextVar set by GuardMiddleware; the access line is logged inside it) and "exc" (the formatted traceback) when there is one. Stdlib only.
  • Redaction: RedactSecretsFilter rewrites the values of the key, api_key and token query parameters to REDACTED in every string of record.args (keeping the args tuple's shape, which uvicorn's AccessFormatter unpacks) and in record.msg. It parses each ?query (up to #, whitespace or "): the query is split on & and a parameter is redacted when its name, percent-decoded (as auth reads it) and lower-cased, is one of the three, so k%65y= and KEY= are masked and step_key= is not; every other parameter stays byte-identical. It sits on uvicorn's handlers (via log_config), on clef's root handler and, from the lifespan, on the uvicorn.access logger, which covers servers started with plain uvicorn. Keys therefore never reach clef's logs; reverse-proxy logs are the operator's (SECURITY.md has Caddy / nginx masking snippets).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Always {"detail": "<message>", "request_id": "<hex>"}; header X-Request-ID on every response. 400 invalid input, 401 auth, 404 unknown classifier / model / job, 409 too many classifiers or jobs (or an invalid job state transition), 413 too large, 429 rate limited (+ Retry-After), 503 not ready / OOM, 500 internal (generic message; traceback only in the server log). The OpenAI and Hugging Face routes use their clients' error shapes (see Compat).

Also: 403 a valid key without the route's scope ({"detail": "key 'ci-bot' lacks scope 'jobs'"}; OpenAI shape permission_denied); 404 also for a model the server does not serve (model_not_found on the OpenAI routes); 429 also for an exhausted daily quota (daily quota exceeded (N records/day), Retry-After = seconds to the next UTC midnight; OpenAI code insufficient_quota). ERRORS in main.py and compat_errors._OPENAI_TYPES/_CODES gain 403.

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text: openapi.json at the repo root is exported from create_app() by scripts/export_openapi.py (--check verifies it is up to date). All routes, including the feature modules', have pydantic request/response models so /docs shows them.

docs.title: CLI (clef, cli.py)
docs.text:
clef serve [--host H] [--port P] [--device D] [--dtype T] [--quant Q] [--offload none|cpu]
           [--max-device-memory-gb GB] [--model-path DIR] [--log-format text|json] [--detach] [--timeout S]
           # flags set the matching CLEF_* env; foreground by default (Ctrl+C stops)
clef stop | clef status [--json] | clef logs [-f] [-n N]
clef doctor [--no-gpu] [--smoke] [--json]    # exit 0 ok/warn, 1 on any FAIL
clef download [--revision SHA] [--dir DIR] [--yes]
clef bench [http_bench args...]              # against the running server
clef open                                    # opens http://<host>:<port>/ in the browser
clef version
- --detach: spawns python -m clef_server.main as a detached process (POSIX start_new_session, Windows DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP), writes paths.pid_file, logs to paths.log_file (rotating the previous log to .1..3), then waits for /livez and for /health status ready|warming (health-gated start, --timeout default 600 s); on exit or status=error prints the last 20 log lines and exits 1. Refuses to start when something already answers on the port. - stop: SIGTERM (Windows: taskkill /PID /T), wait 30 s, then kill; removes the pidfile. - status: process + /health summary (backend, device, status); exit 0 when healthy. - doctor --no-gpu: skips everything that needs a GPU or the weights (smoke check). On a GPU, doctor also prints a memory setting line (from recommend_memory_setting) when bf16 would not fit comfortably. --smoke: loads the model on the detected backend, runs one fixed record, checks probabilities sum to 1 and prints latency. - download: huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(MODEL_REPO, revision=MODEL_REVISION) into the HF cache (or --dir / CLEF_MODEL_PATH), resumable; checks free disk >= 21 GB first and warns about the ~19 GB size. - Wrappers: scripts/launch_server.sh and clef.ps1 are thin wrappers over the CLI; clef.ps1 (Windows -> WSL) keeps the hidden WSL keep-alive session.

docs.title: Console (static/)
docs.text: Zero-build Preact + htm; one vendored charting library (static/vendor/uPlot.*, MIT) for time series, everything else hand-written SVG. No runtime CDN calls. Screens: Playground (SystemOne + Classify modes), History, Batch, Review (routers and the review queue; classifiers scope), Evaluate (labelled dataset -> /v1/classify/batch in chunks -> /v1/evaluate/metrics; confusion heatmap, reliability diagram, coverage curve, mistakes, export), Ops. It consumes /health, /v1/stats, /v1/stats/timeseries, /v1/events?step_s= (read with fetch() and the X-API-Key header, not EventSource, so the key never goes in the URL), /v1/log, /v1/systemone, /v1/batch, /v1/classify, /v1/classify/batch, /v1/classifiers*, /v1/evaluate/metrics.

docs.title: Build contract (v3.2)
docs.text:
The sections below were the contract for the v3.2 build waves (C to F) and are now built: storage, models, keys, cache, review and router, the job scheduler, files and batches, job throughput. Not built: wave G (vLLM and graph capture) and what the sections explicitly mark as later. Where a section says "Supersedes", read it as already applied to the text above.

Rules shared by every section below: - One clef server per database (D3). No leases, no outbox, no cross-process cancel. recover() keeps turning every running job into interrupted at startup. - SQL below is the logical DDL. It is valid on SQLite and Postgres except for identity columns, written BIGINT PRIMARY KEY /* identity */: SQLAlchemy emits INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT on SQLite (sqlite_autoincrement=True) and BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY on Postgres. Timestamps are DOUBLE PRECISION unix seconds (as jobs today), days are TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' (UTC), booleans are INTEGER 0/1, JSON is TEXT, upserts use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (...) DO UPDATE (SQLite >= 3.24). No partial indexes in new tables, no WITHOUT ROWID, no PRAGMA outside db.py. - Every DB call runs in a thread (asyncio.to_thread / run_in_threadpool), never on the event loop. The auth path never touches the DB per request (keys come from an in-memory cache). - Python >= 3.10: datetime.timezone.utc (not datetime.UTC), zoneinfo (plus tzdata on Windows), no StrEnum, no typing.Self. - cli.py stays stdlib-only at import time. clef db, clef backup, clef keys and clef classifiers import clef_server.db / keystore inside the command function and exit 2 with needs the server extra: pip install 'clef-local[server]' when SQLAlchemy is missing. - New tests go in new files named after the workstream (tests/unit/test_db.py, test_models.py, test_keys.py, test_cache.py, test_scheduler.py, test_router.py, test_batches.py); edits to existing test files are limited to what a changed contract forces. - Shared files are edited append-only where possible: new Config fields, AppContext fields, Configuration rows and pyproject.toml entries go at the end of their block under a # <workstream id> comment, so the coordinator can keep both sides of a conflict. openapi.json, uv.lock and CHANGELOG.md are regenerated or merged by the coordinator at the wave merge, never hand-merged.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Module boundary: db.py owns the engine, connections, transactions, migrations and URL handling. dbschema.py owns the table definitions. Stores (JobStore in jobs.py, ClassifierStore in classifiers.py, KeyStore in keystore.py, the router / review / files stores) take a Database and use SQLAlchemy Core (select, insert, update; text() only where Core cannot express it). No ORM. No SQL outside the stores and db.py.

Dependencies: the server extra gains sqlalchemy>=2.0,<2.1 and alembic>=1.13; new extra postgres = ["psycopg[binary]>=3.2", "psycopg-pool>=3.2"]. A Postgres URL without psycopg fails at startup with CLEF_DATABASE_URL is Postgres but psycopg is not installed: pip install 'clef-local[postgres]'.

class DatabaseError(RuntimeError): ...        # bad URL, missing driver, second server on the same DB, failed upgrade

class Database:
    url: str                                   # normalised SQLAlchemy URL (contains the password: never log it)
    display_url: str                           # redact_url(url)
    dialect: str                               # "sqlite" | "postgresql"
    path: Path | None                          # the SQLite file, else None
    def __init__(self, url: str, pool_size: int = 5) -> None
    def tx(self) -> ContextManager[Connection]       # write transaction: BEGIN IMMEDIATE on SQLite (under a process
                                                     # RLock, like JobStore today), BEGIN on Postgres; commit/rollback
    def read(self) -> ContextManager[Connection]     # read-only, no write lock
    def upgrade(self) -> None                        # alembic `upgrade heads`; idempotent
    def schema_version(self) -> str                  # alembic head revision(s), e.g. "0002" ("+"-joined if several)
    def bump(self, conn: Connection, key: str) -> int  # clef_meta counter += 1 inside the caller's tx; returns it
    def meta(self, key: str) -> str | None
    def close(self) -> None

def database_url(cfg: Config) -> str           # CLEF_DATABASE_URL or sqlite:///<state_dir>/clef.db; normalises postgres
def redact_url(url: str) -> str                # postgresql+psycopg://user:***@host:5432/clef
def open_database(cfg: Config) -> Database     # legacy rename -> Database -> PG lock -> upgrade -> classifier import
def audit(conn: Connection, actor: str, action: str, target: str, detail: dict | None = None,
          ip: str | None = None, request_id: str | None = None) -> None   # one audit_log row in the caller's tx

Engine setup: - SQLite: a QueuePool of file connections; a connect event sets journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=30000; writes are serialised by the tx() RLock + BEGIN IMMEDIATE. A new file is created 0600 on POSIX. - Postgres: pool_size=CLEF_DATABASE_POOL_SIZE, max_overflow=pool_size, pool_pre_ping=True. At open, a dedicated connection (its own NullPool engine, libpq TCP keepalives keepalives=1, keepalives_idle=10, keepalives_interval=5, keepalives_count=3; never a pooled connection) takes pg_try_advisory_lock(1667032422) and holds it for the process lifetime; a second server on the same DB fails with DatabaseError("another clef server holds this database (one server per database)"). The CLI commands do not take the lock. - Lock heartbeat (Database.start_heartbeat, started by the lifespan): a daemon thread checks every 10 s, on the lock connection, SELECT 1 FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype = 'advisory' AND pid = pg_backend_pid() AND objid = <key> AND granted (an error counts as lost: the session, and so the lock, is gone). When lost, a second server may already own the DB: it logs CRITICAL, sets lock_lost (tx() then raises DatabaseError, claim_next returns None) and exits the process with status 3 at once (os._exit: no shutdown hooks, which would write), so a supervisor restarts it; the restarted server takes the lock again or stops at startup. - open_database is called once in create_app and published as ctx.db. JobStore, ClassifierStore and the later stores receive it; nothing else opens connections. The lifespan closes ctx.db after the shutdown hooks (runner.stop no longer closes the store).

jobs.db → clef.db (only when CLEF_DATABASE_URL is unset): if <state_dir>/clef.db does not exist and <state_dir>/jobs.db does, jobs.db is copied, never changed in place. Open it with sqlite3 (timeout 1 s), set PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE and run BEGIN EXCLUSIVE; COMMIT (the lock then lasts until close and fails while any other connection, such as a v3.1 server still running, has the file open). If that fails: DatabaseError("jobs.db is in use by another process; stop the old server first"), and nothing is touched. Otherwise remove a stale clef.db.tmp, copy with the sqlite3 online backup API into a new 0600 clef.db.tmp (it reads through jobs.db-wal), fsync it, os.replace it to clef.db and fsync the directory. Then close jobs.db (SQLite checkpoints and removes its WAL) and rename it jobs.db.migrated (.migrated.N if taken; a leftover -wal follows it as jobs.db.migrated-wal, a -shm is deleted). Logged once at INFO. Idempotent: with no jobs.db there is nothing to do. When both files exist: a WARNING, and clef.db is used.

Alembic layout (src/clef_server/migrations/, shipped in the wheel; no alembic.ini, db.py builds the Alembic Config in code):

Revision Creates Owner 0001_baseline jobs, items, jobs_status, jobs_idem exactly as today C1 0002_v32 clef_meta, classifiers, classifier_versions, audit_log, the new jobs columns, api_principals, api_keys, api_usage, routers, router_label_sets, review, llm_calls, files, batches C1 0003_job_hits jobs.hits BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0: the result-cache hits already handed back to the job's quota reservation (E1; review fix: the refund was in memory only) E1
  • Legacy DB (a jobs table, no alembic_version): run today's idem_key ALTER if the column is missing, stamp 0001, then upgrade heads.
  • C1 creates every table in this document in 0002, so waves D to F normally need no migration. A later workstream that must change the schema adds NNNN_<ws>_<what>.py with down_revision = the head at the start of its wave. Two in one wave give two heads: startup always runs upgrade heads (never head), and the coordinator adds an alembic merge revision when merging the wave.
  • dbschema.py mirrors the migrations; a unit test compares metadata with a freshly migrated SQLite DB.

schema_version (= Database.schema_version()) is shown in /health ("db": {"dialect", "schema_version", "url": display_url}), in clef doctor (a database check: connect and report the version; FAIL when the DB is behind or ahead of the code) and by clef db current. No separate table. A database at a revision this code does not know (made by a newer clef) is not touched: upgrade() raises DatabaseError("database schema <rev> is newer than this clef (expects <head>): upgrade clef, or point it at another database") (serve logs it on one line and exits 3, clef db upgrade prints it and exits 1); any other Alembic CommandError becomes a DatabaseError too.

Tables (new or changed by 0002):

CREATE TABLE clef_meta (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT NOT NULL);
-- rows: keys_gen (int, bumped by every key write), classifiers_imported ('1' once the JSON import ran)

ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN model TEXT;                               -- C1: "id@revision" served at submit
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN priority INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;      -- E1: 0 low, 1 normal, 2 high, 3 urgent
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN schedule TEXT;                            -- E1: JSON {"window": "20:00-06:00", "tz": ...}
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN expire_after_s DOUBLE PRECISION;          -- E1: NULL = never expires
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN eligible_at DOUBLE PRECISION;             -- E1: first time the job could take a turn
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN quota_day TEXT;                           -- E1: UTC day the reservation was charged to
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN quota_reserved BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; -- E1: records reserved at submit
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN tokens BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;         -- E1: sum of input_tokens of the stored rows
ALTER TABLE jobs ADD COLUMN hits BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;           -- 0003: cache hits handed back to the quota

CREATE TABLE classifiers (
    name           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,             -- NAME_RE
    owner          TEXT,                         -- principal that created it; NULL = auth off / imported
    latest_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at     DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    updated_at     DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE classifier_versions (
    name       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES classifiers(name) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    version    INTEGER NOT NULL,                 -- 1, 2, ...; never reused while the name exists
    definition TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- JSON ClassifierDef.model_dump() (exactly today's body)
    model      TEXT,                             -- ctx.model_ref() when written
    created_at DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    created_by TEXT,                             -- principal name | "router:<name>" | "cli" | "import"
    PRIMARY KEY (name, version)
);
CREATE TABLE audit_log (
    id         BIGINT PRIMARY KEY /* identity */,
    ts         DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    actor      TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- principal name, "cli:<os user>", "router:<name>", "anonymous"
    action     TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- see the action list below
    target     TEXT NOT NULL,
    detail     TEXT,                             -- JSON; never a secret, never request content
    ip         TEXT,
    request_id TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX audit_ts ON audit_log(ts);

Audit actions: classifier.put, classifier.delete (C1); key.create, key.rotate, key.revoke, principal.update, principal.disable, job.cancel, job.delete (D1); router.put, router.delete, router.activate, review.resolve (E2); batch.cancel, file.delete (F1). The log is append-only; there is no purge in v3.2.

JobStore(db) keeps today's public method set and return shapes (create, find_idem, get, list, payload, set_total, add_items, finish, cancel_queued, flag_cancel, park, park_running, recover, reset_items, delete, purge, items, set_delivery, redeliver, pending_deliveries) and the A2 guarantees (terminal status + pending webhook record in one transaction; add_items reads done inside its transaction). Changes: - next_runnable() + mark_running() become claim_next() -> dict | None: one transaction that selects status IN ('queued','interrupted') ORDER BY CASE WHEN status='interrupted' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, seq LIMIT 1 with .with_for_update(skip_locked=True) (ignored on SQLite, where BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialises) and sets it running. claim(job_id) -> bool is the same conditional update for one id (E1 picks the id itself). - create(..., model: str | None) stores jobs.model. The submit route fills it with ctx.model_ref(); at run time a job whose model differs from ctx.model_ref() fails with job was submitted for <model>, this server serves <ref> (one model per process, D6). model NULL (rows from before v3.2) runs. - Tests must not touch store._db; use store.db.tx() with text().

Classifiers (ClassifierStore(db, max_classifiers)): get(name), list(), put(name, definition), delete(name) keep their return shapes (jobs.py and evaluation.py call them). Extended signatures: 

def get(self, name: str, version: int | None = None) -> dict | None   # latest when version is None
def put(self, name: str, definition: dict, owner: str | None = None, created_by: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None) -> dict           # appends version n+1; a definition equal to the latest is a
                                                    # no-op returning the latest (idempotent PUT); writes audit
def versions(self, name: str) -> list[dict] | None  # [{version, created_at, created_by, model}], newest first
def owner(self, name: str) -> str | None
The returned definition = today's fields + {"version", "owner", "model"}; created_at = version 1, updated_at = latest. CLEF_MAX_CLASSIFIERS counts names. Delete removes the name and all its versions (jobs hold a snapshot). JSON import: once (clef_meta.classifiers_imported), every readable <state_dir>/classifiers/*.json becomes version 1 with owner NULL and created_by import; the directory is then renamed classifiers.imported/. Unreadable files are logged and skipped.

Routes (changes; every existing body stays valid): - PUT /v1/classifiers/{name} -> 200 the definition with version, owner, model. Owner = the caller's principal on the first PUT (NULL with auth off). A later PUT or DELETE by another principal is 403 unless the caller has admin; a classifier whose owner is NULL (created while auth was off, or imported) is admin-only to change or delete once auth is on (running it stays open to classify). The 403 text does not name the owner. The admin test is one helper: the request's principal.has("admin") when request.state.principal is set (D1), else any caller with a key is admin (until D1 lands every key is an env key, and env principals have every scope), so before D1 the owner is recorded but no PUT / DELETE is refused. - GET /v1/classifiers/{name}?version=N; GET /v1/classifiers/{name}/versions -> {"name", "versions": [...]}; GET /v1/classifiers/{name}/versions/{v} -> that definition. 404 for an unknown name or version. - POST /v1/classifiers/{name}[/batch], and the classifier field of jobs and POST /v1/evaluate, accept an optional "version": int (default latest). Job snapshots record the version they copied (payload.classifier_version).

CLI (direct DB access through CLEF_DATABASE_URL or the default file; works with the server stopped): 

clef db current                          # schema version and display URL
clef db upgrade                          # alembic upgrade heads (the server also does it at startup)
clef db copy --from URL --to URL [--yes] # every table in FK order, 1000 rows per batch; the target is upgraded
                                         # first and must be empty (exit 1 otherwise); Postgres identity sequences
                                         # are reset (setval to max); refuses while a server answers on the port
clef backup [--out PATH]                 # SQLite: the sqlite3 online backup API into
                                         # <state_dir>/backups/clef-<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>.db (file 0600; safe
                                         # while the server runs); Postgres: exit 2 with a pg_dump hint
clef classifiers export [--out DIR] [--name N]   # latest version of each as <DIR>/<name>.json (today's file format
                                                 # + "version"); default DIR ./classifiers

Error codes: 403 (not the owner), 404 (unknown version), 409 (CLEF_MAX_CLASSIFIERS), 503 database unavailable (DatabaseError and SQLAlchemy OperationalError: an exception handler registered in create_app, plus the classifier routes, which map them before map_exception; map_exception itself stays C2's hunk).

Invariants: payload columns stay out of list selects (the _COLS discipline); store APIs are sync; one writer transaction at a time on SQLite; the request path reaches the DB only through stores called in the threadpool.

As built (C1; additions to the interface above, nothing in it changed): - Database also has serialize(conn, name) (inside tx(): a transaction advisory lock on Postgres for check-then-write sections such as CLEF_MAX_JOBS / CLEF_MAX_CLASSIFIERS; a no-op on SQLite, where BEGIN IMMEDIATE already serialises), set_meta(conn, key, value), acquire_server_lock() (called by open_database) and info() (the cached /health block; no I/O). Nested tx() / read() on the same thread join the open transaction. db.py also holds the CLI / doctor helpers (peek_version opens nothing for writing, version_state, copy_database, backup_sqlite, migrate_legacy_file) and is_unavailable(exc). - claim_next() returns the running row plus claimed_from ("queued" | "interrupted", the status before the claim); run_base_done is set to done by the claim and zeroed by reset_items. The runner seeds cancel_ids from the claimed row and never discards an id after a claim. JobStore.close() closes its Database (tests); the server never calls it. The scheduler claims with claim(job_id); when that raises (possibly after its commit) the runner parks only that id, never park_running(), which stays for the clean stop after every job task has ended. - ClassifierStore.put / delete take keyword-only actor, ip, request_id for the audit row (actor defaults to created_by, then "anonymous"). The JSON import writes classifier.put rows with actor import. - ClassifierStore.put first takes db.serialize(conn, "classifier:<name>") (on Postgres a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on a name that does not exist yet locks nothing, so two first PUTs would both insert version 1), then reads the head. It also takes a keyword-only check_owner(current_owner) callback, called inside that transaction (None for a new name) that raises to refuse: the PUT route passes its 403 check there, so the ownership check and the append are atomic. DELETE still checks before its own transaction. - AppContext.model_ref() / check_model() are methods (they read the engine's hooks at call time). - Job payloads of classify / score accept version next to classifier; the snapshot drops it and records classifier_version. EvaluateRequest has both fields too. - The alembic logger is set to WARNING; upgrade() logs database: schema <from> -> <to> at INFO when it changed something.

Superseded (applied): "Storage: SQLite <state_dir>/jobs.db" in Async jobs, the classifiers.py row of the package layout, and the "Files: <state_dir>/classifiers/<name>.json" bullet in Saved classifiers.

docs.title: Decision model interface
docs.text:
Scope (D5, D6, D13, D14): one model per process, chosen by CLEF_MODEL and a restart. v3.2 ships one adapter, clef-release, which serves every Cloudflare-style release (joint_schema_model.py + joint_head.* next to the weights): clef-flash and clef (27B). Not in v3.2: hf-label-lm, encoders, remote adapters, several models at once, hot-swap, falling back to the default model for an unknown id. The interface stays generic enough to add them.

Module boundary: models/base.py and models/registry.py are torch-free at import. models/clef_release.py imports torch lazily (inside load and the tensor methods). The engine (engine.py) owns the worker thread, the two priority lanes (A3), micro-batching, bucketing, padding, warmup, OOM handling and stats; it calls the adapter for everything model-specific. offload.py keeps plan_layers / LayerStreamer and takes the layer names from the adapter's OffloadLayout. backend.py stays the only device code.

# models/base.py
class UnknownModel(LookupError): ...          # -> 404 (`model_not_found` on the OpenAI routes)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Capabilities:
    question_types: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"choice", "score", "noul"})
    joint_questions: bool = True              # all questions of a record in ONE forward
    images: bool = False
    videos: bool = False
    max_tokens: int = 16384                   # hard input limit
    max_options: int | None = None            # None = CLEF_MAX_LABELS
    calibrated: str = "trained"               # "trained" | "temperature-fitted" | "raw" | "unknown"
    supports_offload: bool = False
    quant: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"none"})
    optional_kernels: tuple[str, ...] = ()    # ("fla", "causal_conv1d") for Qwen3.5 hybrids

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelSpec:
    id: str                                   # public id: "clef-flash", "clef"
    adapter: str                              # entry-point name: "clef-release"
    repo: str | None                          # HF repo, e.g. "Cloudflare/clef-flash"
    revision: str | None                      # full 40-char sha (pinned), or None for a local dir
    weights_gb: float                         # catalog estimate; the adapter reads the real size at load
    options: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    @property
    def ref(self) -> str                      # f"{id}@{revision or 'local'}"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OffloadLayout:
    layers_prefix: str                        # "model.language_model.layers."
    embed_key: str                            # "model.language_model.embed_tokens"
    head_key: str                             # "lm_head"
    device_prefixes: tuple[str, ...]          # kept on the device: vision tower, final norm, rotary (the joint
                                              # head is not in the device_map: its own module, always on device)

class Encoded(Protocol):                      # opaque to the engine except these
    length: int                               # real tokens (bucketing, usage.input_tokens)
    is_media: bool                            # media records run alone and unpadded
    questions: Sequence[Any]                  # each has .question_id and .option_ids

class DecisionModel(Protocol):
    name: ClassVar[str]                       # adapter (entry-point) name
    files: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ()     # files a complete local release has (`clef doctor` checks them)
    spec: ModelSpec
    capabilities: Capabilities
    @classmethod
    def catalog(cls) -> list[ModelSpec]       # the ids this adapter serves out of the box
    def __init__(self, spec: ModelSpec, cfg: Config) -> None
    def resolve(self) -> Path                 # local weights dir; never downloads; paths.ModelNotFound with a hint
    def weights_gb(self, path: Path) -> float # from the safetensors headers
    def load(self, backend: Backend, dtype: Any) -> LoadInfo   # worker thread: standard / quantized / offloaded
    def validate(self, record: Record) -> None  # capability check, ValueError (400) naming the field
    def info(self) -> dict                    # {"id", "adapter", "revision", "ref", "capabilities"} (JSON:
                                              # the frozensets become sorted lists)

class LocalTensorAdapter(DecisionModel):     # what the engine drives
    def encode(self, record: Record) -> Encoded         # any thread (holds its own tokenizer lock);
                                                        # raises engine.InputTooLarge (the string match lives here)
    def collate(self, encs: list[Encoded], pad_to: int | None) -> dict
