        # CPU batch: {"input_ids", "attention_mask", "media", "lengths": list[int]}; right-padded to pad_to
        # (None for media records); "lengths" are the real lengths, known on the CPU (no .item())
    def to_device(self, batch: dict, device: Any) -> dict
    def forward(self, batch: dict) -> list[list[Any]]   # worker thread, inside torch.inference_mode():
                                                        # per record, per question, the option logits
    def answer(self, q: Any, question: dict, logits: Any) -> dict
        # one question: q = an element of enc.questions (.question_id, .option_ids), question = the record's
        # question dict, logits = that question's option logits from forward(). SystemOne answer (softmax inside)
    def pad_id(self) -> int
    def warm_record(self, repeats: int) -> Record
    def offload_layout(self) -> OffloadLayout | None

Registry (models/registry.py): 

def adapters() -> dict[str, type[DecisionModel]]   # importlib.metadata.entry_points(group="clef.models")
def catalog() -> dict[str, ModelSpec]              # union of adapter catalogs; duplicate id -> the built-in wins + WARNING
def resolve_spec(cfg: Config) -> ModelSpec         # CLEF_MODEL + the legacy aliases (rules below); UnknownModel
def create(cfg: Config) -> DecisionModel
- pyproject.toml: [project.entry-points."clef.models"] clef-release = "clef_server.models.clef_release:ClefReleaseAdapter". Built-ins register exactly like third-party adapters (D14). Entry points are only read from installed distributions; the adapter that loaded and its distribution version go in /health and the startup log. One fallback: when the clef-release entry point is missing (a source checkout on PYTHONPATH, or an install made before the entry point existed), adapters() registers the built-in directly and logs a WARNING (re-install to silence it). Without it, every such checkout would fail to load any model. An entry point that fails to import is skipped with a WARNING. A built-in name (clef-release) is only taken from an entry point whose value is the built-in ref (registry.BUILTIN); any other entry point with that name is ignored with a WARNING, even when the built-in's own entry point is missing, so a third-party package cannot take over clef-release. - Catalog (ClefReleaseAdapter.catalog()): clef-flash → Cloudflare/clef-flash@<MODEL_REVISION> (today's pin, weights_gb 19.0); clef → Cloudflare/clef@<sha> with the full sha taken by C2 from the HF API (never typed from memory), weights_gb from its index. - Loading joint_schema_model.py uses importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("clef_release_<sha8>", path), so the module name no longer collides.

CLEF_MODEL and the old variables (precedence, checked in Config.__post_init__, ValueError on a conflict): 1. CLEF_MODEL=<id>[@<rev>] selects the catalog entry; unset = clef-flash, except that an unset CLEF_MODEL with a CLEF_MODEL_REPO equal to a catalog entry's repo selects that entry. 2. @<rev> overrides the pinned revision. CLEF_MODEL_REVISION is an alias for it; both set and different is an error. 3. CLEF_MODEL_REPO overrides the entry's repo (download source + cache lookup). 4. CLEF_MODEL_PATH is the local release dir for the selected entry (no download, no cache lookup); its ref is <id>@<rev> when a revision was given, else <id>@local. An id that is not in the catalog is an engine load error (status error, message listing the known ids), not a crash; clef doctor reports it as FAIL.

Engine (changes to the interface above; Engine(cfg, stats, loader=None, backend=None, model=None)): 

class Engine:
    model: DecisionModel | None        # set on the worker thread at load; test injection via `model=`
    spec: ModelSpec                    # resolved at construction (torch-free)
    def model_ref(self) -> str         # spec.ref
    def check_model(self, requested: str | None) -> str
        # None / "" -> spec.id. Accepted: spec.id, spec.ref (e.g. "clef-flash@local"), spec.repo,
        # f"{spec.id}@{rev}" (full sha or a >= 7-char prefix).
        # Anything else -> UnknownModel(f"model {requested!r} is not served here (this server serves {spec.id!r})")
    def validate(self, record: Record) -> None
        # the loaded model's capability check (ValueError -> 400); media need only be present, not decoded.
        # main.py's prepare runs it per request after check_limits and BEFORE media decode, prefixing
        # "<label>[i]." in batches (e.g. "batch[1].questions.d.criteria: too many options (max 64)")
    async def prepare(self, records: list[Record], cache: bool = True) -> Prepared
        # validate + check_model per record, cache lookup (D3; no-op until then), encode the misses in threads
    async def submit(self, prepared: Prepared, priority: str = "interactive") -> list[Result]
        # enqueue the misses in the lane, await, fill the cache, merge hits back in input order
    async def decide(self, records: list[Record], priority: str = "interactive", cache: bool = True) -> list[Result]
        # = submit(await prepare(records, cache), priority); unchanged for every existing caller

@dataclass
class Prepared:
    records: list[Record]
    keys: list[str | None]             # cache keys; None = not cacheable (filled by D3)
    hits: dict[int, Result]            # index -> cached result (filled by D3)
    encoded: list[Encoded | None]      # None at hit positions
    def slice(self, start: int, stop: int) -> Prepared   # for bisection in decide_resilient
- Compatibility: Engine(cfg, stats, loader=fn) still accepts the test namespace (load_release_model, encode_record, collate_records, systemone_answer); it is wrapped with ClefReleaseAdapter.from_module(...). clef_server.engine keeps exporting the names tests patch: load_model, _load_offloaded, _embeddings_to_host, backend_mod, bucket_for, pad_batch_right, LoadInfo, device_budget_gb, _import_model_module, and the attributes _load_info, _thread. - Results echo model = spec.id (no longer the requested string). usage and timing are unchanged. - The priority lane stays in the engine, above the adapter: the lanes hold _Items carrying Encoded, and the worker calls collate → to_device → forward → answer for each length group. The offload layer is set up inside adapter.load() (it calls engine.load_model / offload.plan_layers with its OffloadLayout); the engine only resets the streamer after a failed forward (LoadInfo.streamer.reset()). - paths.WEIGHTS_GB, MIN_FREE_GB (cli) and doctor's file list come from the selected spec / adapter.

Perf hooks (D2, F2, wave G; nothing here changes probabilities by itself): - D2 works inside ClefReleaseAdapter.forward and its head: with CLEF_MASK_FREE=1 a text-only batch calls the backbone with attention_mask=None and the head slices by batch["lengths"] (sync-free, vectorised). Media batches keep the mask. Gate: bench/parity.py (max |dp| within the fp16 noise floor, 0 flips). - TunableOp results are kept per model: PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_FILENAME under <state_dir>/tunableop/<spec.id>@<rev8>/ (set by backend.prepare_environment from CLEF_MODEL, through registry.model_slug(environ): the resolve_spec rules over the built-in catalog, so CLEF_MODEL_REPO=Cloudflare/clef alone gives the 27B's slug; @local with CLEF_MODEL_PATH and no revision). - Graph capture (wave G) belongs in forward, keyed by (batch["input_ids"].shape); warmup already visits every bucket <= 1024 at batch sizes {1, max_microbatch}. - F2 tokenizes ahead with ctx.prepare (below): encoding is not "in flight"; only submit enqueues.

AppContext additions (C2): prepare(reqs, batch=True, label="batch", cache=True) -> Prepared (limits, media, engine.prepare) and decide_prepared(prepared, priority="background") -> list[Result]. ctx.decide(...) gains cache: bool = True and equals decide_prepared(await prepare(...)). C1 adds model_ref() -> str | None and check_model(requested) -> str, wired to the engine's methods when it has them (test fakes fall back to None / returning requested or "clef-flash").

API changes: - model on every request body (SystemOne, classify, score, classifiers, jobs payloads, chat, evaluate) defaults to None = the served model. A model the server does not serve is 404 before any inference: {"detail": "model 'x' is not served here (this server serves 'clef-flash')"}; OpenAI routes {"error": {"type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "model_not_found", "param": "model"}}. /v1/chat/completions no longer lists model in clef.ignored. - Jobs validate every model in the payload at submit (404), and store jobs.model = ctx.model_ref() (C1). - POST /v1/evaluate and the evaluate job kind accept model (validated the same way). - GET /v1/models lists the one served model: {"id": spec.id, "object": "model", "created", "owned_by": "cloudflare", "clef": {"adapter", "revision", "ref", "status", "capabilities"}}; GET /v1/models/{id} accepts the same strings as check_model, else 404 model_not_found. - POST /hf/models/{id}: the path id is still ignored (Hugging Face clients send their own model names); responses report spec.id. - /health gains "model": engine.model.info() (or the spec before load). The fast_path block stays (filled from capabilities.optional_kernels). - clef download [--model ID[@REV]] (default: the selected spec), clef models (catalog + installed adapters, marking the selected one; --json). - Clients and console stop hard-coding "clef-flash": they omit model unless the user sets one, and the console shows the id from /v1/models.

Tables: none (the model ref is stored on jobs.model and classifier_versions.model, see Storage).

Error codes: 404 unknown model; 400 capability mismatch (images to a text-only model, a question type the adapter lacks, more options than max_options); 413 InputTooLarge; 503 not ready / OOM (unchanged).

Invariants: ONE GPU worker thread, ONE adapter per process; the adapter never edits files in the model dir; every result for a record is computed by exactly one forward call (cache hits excepted).

As built (C2), beyond the text above: - Engine.model_info() (the adapter's info() or the spec before the load, plus distribution: the adapter's <dist> <version>) feeds /health model and the clef block of /v1/models; Engine.capabilities() feeds fast_path. Engine.model is set only after a successful load (prepare / submit raise EngineNotReady before). - "model": null is accepted and means the served model (schemas.DEFAULT_MODEL is None; clients omit the field). - models.registry.served_model(engine, requested) is the check main.py, compat_openai and evaluation use: it calls engine.check_model and, for test engines without one, returns requested or "clef-flash". - Capability validation applies max_options (= CLEF_MAX_LABELS, 64) to /v1/systemone questions too, so a choice / score question with more options is now a 400 there as well. - ClefReleaseAdapter.encode returns ReleaseEncoded(raw, length, is_media), which also exposes input_ids / media for the bench scripts; collate keeps the release's "records" key (its head reads it). - The 27B catalog entry is Cloudflare/clef@0b331204bb13fbd2ca93a64df1956f5b55478ce5 (HF API sha, 2026-10-17), weights_gb 55.0 (index total_size + joint head, measured like clef-flash's 19.0), and carries options["fits_24gb"] = "nf4", which clef doctor turns into its WARN (also with --no-gpu). - The TunableOp directory is created by the engine before the load (prepare_environment does no I/O). - Saved-classifier runs (/v1/classifiers/{name}[/batch]) take model from the request body.

Superseded (applied): "ONE uvicorn worker per process (one model)" (now "one model adapter"), "GET /v1/models lists clef-flash" and "model defaults to "clef-flash"" in the Classification and Compat sections. The load_release_model wording in Engine interface stays: the engine still calls the release's load_release_model.

docs.title: Keys and principals
docs.text:
Model: a principal is a name with scopes, a daily quota and a status; it owns jobs, classifiers, routers, files and batches (all keyed by name, as jobs.owner is today). A principal has 1 to 5 active keys (overlapping rotation). Env keys (CLEF_API_KEY, CLEF_API_KEYS, name:key kept) are principals with source="env", every scope (full admin), no quota and the global rate limit (break-glass + bootstrap, D10).

Module boundary: keystore.py (schema access through db.py, key generation / parsing / hashing, CRUD, the in-memory KeyCache, Quotas) is shared by the server and clef keys. security.py keeps CORS, the rate limiter and RedactSecretsFilter, and gains Authenticator (env + DB resolution) and require_scope. admin.py is the feature module with the routes.

Key format: clef_live_<id>_<secret>: id = 12 chars [a-z2-7] (public, shown in lists); secret = secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (43 chars, may contain _ and -); 66 chars total. Parse by fixed offsets (prefix clef_live_, id = s[10:22], s[22] == "_", secret = s[23:]), never by splitting on _. Only sha256(whole string) (hex) is stored. Lists show clef_live_<id>_…. The secret is returned once, at create / rotate.

Tables (created by C1 in 0002): 

CREATE TABLE api_principals (
    name        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                -- KEY_NAME_RE; also jobs.owner
    scopes      TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- sorted, comma-separated: "classify,jobs"
    daily_quota BIGINT,                          -- records per UTC day; NULL = unlimited
    rate_limit  INTEGER,                         -- requests/min; NULL = CLEF_RATE_LIMIT
    note        TEXT,
    created_at  DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    created_by  TEXT,                            -- principal name or "cli:<os user>"
    disabled_at DOUBLE PRECISION                 -- tombstone: rows are never deleted, names never reused
);
CREATE TABLE api_keys (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,              -- the 12-char public id
    principal     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES api_principals(name),
    secret_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at    DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    created_by    TEXT,
    expires_at    DOUBLE PRECISION,              -- NULL = never; rotate sets now + grace on the old keys
    revoked_at    DOUBLE PRECISION,
    last_used_at  DOUBLE PRECISION               -- approximate, flushed every 10 s
);
CREATE INDEX api_keys_principal ON api_keys(principal);
CREATE TABLE api_usage (
    principal TEXT NOT NULL,
    day       TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- 'YYYY-MM-DD' UTC
    records   BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,         -- interactive records + job reservations (net of refunds)
    requests  BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    rejected  BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,         -- requests refused for quota
    PRIMARY KEY (principal, day)
);
Every write to api_principals / api_keys bumps clef_meta.keys_gen in the same transaction, except the last_used_at flush (it would reload every cache every 10 s under traffic). Key actions are written to audit_log (Storage) in the same transaction. CORS (security.install_cors) gains PATCH in allow_methods and X-Quota-Limit, X-Quota-Remaining in expose_headers.

Scopes: classify, jobs, classifiers, ops, admin, urgent. admin implies all the others.

Routes Scope POST /v1/systemone, /v1/batch, /v1/classify[/batch], /v1/score, POST /v1/classifiers/{n}[/batch], GET /v1/classifiers*, GET /v1/models*, POST /v1/chat/completions, /hf/models/*, /models/*, POST /v1/evaluate[/metrics], POST /v1/routers/{n}/route[/batch] classify /v1/jobs*, /v1/files*, /v1/batches* jobs (submitting needs only jobs) PUT / DELETE /v1/classifiers/{n}, /v1/routers* except route, /v1/review* classifiers GET /v1/stats*, /v1/log, /v1/events ops /v1/admin/* admin urgent: true on a job or batch urgent (403 otherwise) GET /v1/whoami any valid key

Admins see every principal's jobs, files, batches, routers and review items (D19). A default-deny unit test walks app.routes and fails when a /v1/*, /hf/* or /models/* route has no scope dependency.

ALL_SCOPES = frozenset({"classify", "jobs", "classifiers", "ops", "admin", "urgent"})

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Principal:
    name: str
    source: str                          # "env" | "db"
    scopes: frozenset[str]               # env: ALL_SCOPES
    daily_quota: int | None              # env: None
    rate_limit: int | None               # None = CLEF_RATE_LIMIT
    key_id: str | None                   # env: None
    expires_at: float | None
    def has(self, scope: str) -> bool    # "admin" in scopes or scope in scopes

class Authenticator:                     # security.py
    def __init__(self, env_keys: dict[str, str], cache: KeyCache | None): ...
    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool            # env keys exist OR any api_principals row exists (even disabled), so
                                         # revoking the last DB key never switches auth off
    def resolve(self, token: str | None) -> Principal | None
        # 1. token has the clef_live_ format and its id is cached: compare sha256 (hmac.compare_digest), then
        #    check revoked_at, expires_at (against now, at request time) and the principal's disabled_at.
        # 2. otherwise the constant-time walk over env keys (as KeyAuth does today).
        # 3. else None (-> 401).

class KeyCache:                          # keystore.py; no DB I/O on the request path
    def __init__(self, db: Database, refresh_s: float = 10.0): ...
    def get(self, key_id: str) -> tuple[KeyRow, PrincipalRow] | None
    def any_principal(self) -> bool
    def reload(self) -> None             # full reload (a few hundred rows)
    async def run(self) -> None          # ctx.on_startup task: every 10 s read clef_meta.keys_gen in a thread and
                                         # reload when it changed; full reload every 60 s regardless
    # admin API writes call reload() synchronously, so they apply at once; CLI writes apply within 10 s

class QuotaExceeded(Exception):
    limit: int; remaining: int; retry_after: int   # seconds to the next UTC midnight

class Quotas:                            # keystore.py; in-memory and authoritative (one server per DB)
    def reserve(self, principal: Principal | None, n: int) -> Reservation | None
        # None for env principals / auth off. A DB principal without a quota still gets a Reservation: usage is
        # counted (Keys tab, used_today) but never refused. Raises QuotaExceeded when daily_quota is set and
        # used_today + n > daily_quota. Records the reservation on today's UTC row at once.
    def remaining(self, principal: Principal | None) -> tuple[int, int] | None   # (limit, left); None = no quota
    def refund(self, reservation: Reservation, n: int) -> None   # n <= reservation.n; same day row
    def used(self, name: str, day: str | None = None) -> int
    def reject(self, name: str) -> None                          # api_usage.rejected += 1
    async def run(self) -> None          # ctx.on_startup: load today's rows, flush deltas every 5 s (UPSERT in a
                                         # thread), and once more on shutdown; a crash loses at most 5 s of counts

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reservation:
    principal: str; day: str; n: int

Request path: require_key sets request.state.principal (or None with auth off) and keeps request.state.key_name = principal.name (log, by_key, job owner, rate-limit identity unchanged). The rate limiter uses principal.rate_limit or CLEF_RATE_LIMIT. ctx.infer calls ctx.quotas.reserve(principal, len(reqs)) before inference and refunds the whole reservation when the request ends in an error (nothing was computed for a 4xx raised before the engine either; a partly computed failure is rare enough to ignore). Cache hits do NOT count: the reservation is settled after the cache lookup (ctx.prepare) and only computed records are charged (hits cost no GPU time). Every response of a quota'd principal to a route that reserves carries X-Quota-Limit and X-Quota-Remaining (also on the 429; CORS exposes them). Over quota: 429 daily quota exceeded (N records/day) + Retry-After (OpenAI shape insufficient_quota). Jobs reserve at submit (Job scheduler).

AppContext additions (D1): scope(name: str) -> list[Depends], principal(request) -> Principal | None, quotas: Quotas, auth_enabled() -> bool (replaces cfg.auth_required in jobs.scoped(), /health limits and the bind warning, which moves into the lifespan because it needs the DB).

Routes (admin.py; all pydantic; all admin except whoami; rate limited, never quota'd; admin routes need a principal even when auth is off: 401 admin routes need a key: set CLEF_API_KEY or run clef keys create):

Route Body Response GET /v1/whoami {"auth": bool, "name", "source", "scopes": [...], "daily_quota", "used_today", "key_id", "expires_at"} (all null with auth off) GET /v1/admin/keys?include_disabled=false {"principals": [{"name", "source", "scopes", "daily_quota", "rate_limit", "note", "created_at", "created_by", "disabled_at", "used_today", "keys": [{"id", "display", "created_at", "expires_at", "revoked_at", "last_used_at", "status": "active|expiring|expired|revoked"}]}]}; env principals listed read-only with keys: [] POST /v1/admin/keys {"name", "scopes": [...], "daily_quota"?, "rate_limit"?, "expires_in_days"?, "note"?} 201 principal + {"key": "clef_live_..."} PATCH /v1/admin/keys/{name} {"scopes"?, "daily_quota"?, "rate_limit"?, "note"?} (explicit null clears quota / rate limit) principal POST /v1/admin/keys/{name}/rotate {"grace_s": 86400, "expires_in_days"?} 201 principal + {"key"}; the other active keys get expires_at = min(current, now + grace_s) in one tx POST /v1/admin/keys/{name}/revoke {"key_id"?} principal; without key_id the principal is disabled and all its keys revoked GET /v1/admin/keys/{name}/usage?days=30 {"name", "days": [{"day", "records", "requests", "rejected"}]} oldest first, days 1..366 GET /v1/admin/audit?limit=100&before=<id>&action=<prefix> {"entries": [{"id", "ts", "actor", "action", "target", "detail", "ip", "request_id"}], "next_before": id | null} newest first, limit 1..1000

Errors: 400 bad name (KEY_NAME_RE) or unknown scope; 404 unknown principal or key id; 409 name exists, is a tombstone (disabled names are never reused, D19), or equals an env key name; 409 a 6th active key; 403 changing an env principal that has no DB row of the same name, or a DB admin removing its own admin scope / revoking its own last key without ?force=true. A DB principal whose name equals an env key name is refused: Authenticator.resolve answers 401 for its keys (otherwise it would inherit the env principal's job / classifier ownership and rate-limit bucket), and startup logs a WARNING naming the clash (fix: clef keys revoke NAME or rename the env key). The admin API and the CLI still act on that DB row (revoke, rotate, update), so it can be cleaned up; a pure env key stays read-only. The server is the authority: the CLI reads the env of the shell it runs in, which can differ from the server's, and the server decides at request time.

CLI (clef keys, direct DB, works with the server stopped; the first DB principal turns auth on and the command prints auth is now required for every /v1 route; secrets are printed once): 

clef keys create NAME --scope classify,jobs [--quota N] [--rate-limit N] [--expires 90d|2027-01-31] [--note T] [--json]
clef keys list [--all] [--json]
clef keys rotate NAME [--grace 24h] [--json]
clef keys revoke NAME [--key-id ID]
clef keys update NAME [--scope S] [--quota N|none] [--rate-limit N|none] [--note T]
clef keys usage NAME [--days 30] [--json]
Audit actor for CLI writes: cli:<os user>.

Console: Settings calls GET /v1/whoami after a key is saved and shows name (env|db) · scopes · used/quota. A Keys tab (static/screens/keys.js) is added to TABS only when the scopes include admin: principals table (scope chips, quota bar, 30-day usage sparkline in hand-written SVG, keys with status badges), New key dialog, secret-once panel (copy button; the secret is never stored in the store, history or localStorage), rotate (grace picker), revoke (type the name to confirm), edit, audit list, env principals read-only.

Invariants: no plaintext secret is ever stored or logged; the request path does no DB I/O for auth; a principal row is never deleted; env keys always work and are always admin; auth, once on because of a DB principal, never turns off by itself.

As built (D1; additions and deviations, nothing above changed in meaning): - Principal, ALL_SCOPES and the key helpers live in keystore.py; security.Authenticator composes the old KeyAuth (kept, now only the constant-time env walk) with the KeyCache. - ctx.scope(*names) returns one dependency that also runs require_key; no names = any valid key (/v1/whoami). The callable carries clef_scope = names: the default-deny test (tests/unit/test_keys.py) looks for it on every /v1/*, /hf/*, /models/* route (newer FastAPI keeps included routers lazy, so it walks effective_route_contexts()). New routes in other workstreams (E2's routers and review, F1's files and batches) fail that test until they use ctx.scope. - Wiring: create_app builds KeyCache and Quotas and loads both synchronously (auth is right from the first request, also in tests that never start the lifespan). Their background tasks start from the first on_startup hook (so recover() in jobs can refund into loaded counters) and stop from the last-running on_shutdown hook, which flushes usage and last_used_at. A failed reload keeps the last good cache. - Quotas: reserve returns a Reservation for every DB principal (usage is counted even without a quota) and counts requests / rejected itself. The flush is UPDATE-then-INSERT per row in one transaction (portable; a refund below the stored count clamps at 0), not a dialect upsert. history(name, days) is zero-filled and merges unflushed deltas; remaining(principal) feeds the headers. flush holds a dedicated lock for the whole write, so the shutdown flush waits for a periodic one still running and never writes the same delta twice. Quota counters live in one process's memory, so they are exact only because the Postgres advisory lock (PG_LOCK_KEY, see Database) refuses a second server on the same database; SQLite is one file in one state dir. Do not bypass the lock (for example by running two servers against one database). - ctx.infer: reserve len(reqs) before any work (429 insufficient_quota), ctx.prepare (cache lookup), refund len(prepared.hits), then decide_prepared. Any exception (4xx before the engine included) refunds what is still held. Headers come from request.state.quota, added by GuardMiddleware for every route. - Jobs: JobStore.create(..., quota_day, quota_reserved); the count per kind is jobs.job_records (a kind may give "records": fn(parsed)). JobStore.settle_quota(job_id=None) refunds quota_reserved - done of failed / cancelled jobs once (it then sets quota_reserved = done, the net charge). The runner calls it after every failed / cancelled finish and for all jobs at startup. Cache hits inside jobs are not refunded (the whole job is reserved at submit); E1 may refine that. job.cancel is audited after the cancel, job.delete in the delete's own transaction. Admins see every job (scoped = auth_enabled and not admin). - ApiError has an optional code (OpenAI insufficient_quota; type insufficient_quota too); 403 renders as permission_denied. - bind_warning(cfg, auth_enabled) runs in the lifespan and mentions clef keys create. - CLI: clef keys also has update and usage; --expires takes 90d or a date (valid through that UTC day).

Supersedes when landed: the Keys bullet of "Auth, rate limit, CORS" (KeyAuth, "auth off -> key is null"), the security.py row's "multi-key auth", and "jobs created while auth was off stay visible to every key" (no longer: owner-less jobs are admin-only) plus "other keys get 404" (admins now see all).

docs.title: Result cache
docs.text:
Module boundary: cache.py holds ResultCache; the engine owns the only instance (Engine.cache, built from cfg.cache_size in __init__) and uses it in Engine.prepare (lookup) and Engine.submit (store). Nothing else reads or writes it, so interactive routes, jobs, evaluate, batches and the router all share it (D16).

class ResultCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 10000, max_bytes: int = 256 << 20) -> None  # capacity or max_bytes 0 = disabled
    enabled: bool
    @staticmethod
    def key(model_ref: str, record: Record) -> str | None
        # None (not cacheable) when the record has images or videos.
        # Else sha256 hex of canonical JSON (sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False) of
        # {"m": model_ref, "s": record["state"], "q": [[qid, question], ...]}: the state verbatim (the release sorts
        # it), the questions as an ORDERED list with each choice `criteria` as an ordered [[key, text], ...] list,
        # because the release lays out questions and options in dict order (a different order is a different forward). `model_ref` is `<id>@<revision>`. Thresholds, the request id and the
        # label order of a multi-label response are applied after the model and are not in the key.
    def get(self, key: str) -> Result | None             # a private copy; moves the entry to the MRU end
    def put(self, key: str, result: Result) -> None       # stores a copy without "timing"; evicts the LRU entry
    def note_bypass(self, n: int = 1) -> None             # counts lookups skipped (no-cache, media)
    def clear(self) -> None
    def stats(self) -> dict   # {"enabled", "size", "capacity", "bytes", "max_bytes", "hits", "misses", "bypassed", "evictions"}

Semantics: - Bounds: CLEF_CACHE_SIZE entries and CLEF_CACHE_MB bytes (running estimate: len(json.dumps(stored))). put evicts LRU entries until both hold and skips an entry larger than 1/10 of the byte budget. Memory is about the budget (default 256 MiB at most; typical entries are 1-2 KB so 10000 entries are tens of MB). - Thread-safe (threading.Lock); in memory only, lost on restart. No invalidation: the questions and the model ref are in the key, and the engine also clears the cache when its model loads. - A hit returns a copy of the stored result with usage as stored (the original input_tokens) and timing = {"queue_ms": 0, "forward_ms": 0, "batch_size": 0, "cached": true} (main adds total_ms). Computed records carry "cached": false. timing.cached is the per-record hit marker for quotas and the request log. Probabilities are bit-identical to the stored forward. - Bypass: a request with Cache-Control: no-cache (case-insensitive token anywhere in the header) skips the lookup and still stores the fresh result. ctx.infer reads the header and passes cache=False down (ctx.decide(..., cache=False) -> engine.prepare(records, cache=False)); background callers pass it explicitly. - Identical records inside one call are computed once; the later ones are filled from the first after the forward and are marked as hits and counted as hits in the stats (Prepared.dups; Prepared.slice turns a dup whose source was sliced away into a miss). - Only successful forwards are stored (submit stores them even if a sibling failed). Errors, OOM and media records are never cached. - Quotas (contract decision 3): cache hits do not count. D1 charges only the results whose timing.cached is false. The request log and stats count the request as usual. - /v1/stats gains "cache": Engine.cache_stats() + {"hit_rate"}. The engine registers cache_stats with Stats.set_cache_source at construction; Stats.snapshot reads it. hit_rate = hits / (hits + misses). - Memory: about 2 KB per entry for a 10-option question (measured, ~20 MB for 10 000 entries); more questions or options scale it linearly.

Env: CLEF_CACHE_SIZE (Configuration). Tables: none. Routes: none (header only). Error codes: none.

Invariants: a cache entry is only ever written from a successful forward of the same process; media records never hit the cache; the key never contains secrets or the API key.

docs.title: Review queue and router
docs.text:
Scope (D7, D8, D15, D17, D19): a router is its own resource that grows the label set of one single-label saved classifier. It runs in review mode (default) or auto mode, only adds labels (grow-only; no merge, split, rename or retire in v3.2), and publishes each new label set as a new classifier version. One Review table and one console screen hold both router proposals and low-confidence items; human labels given there feed the router's re-checks.

Module boundary: router.py is the feature module (routes, buffers, flush loop, publishing, the Review routes); its pure logic (gate, "other" description, proposal validation, lexical dedup, acceptance test over a supplied decide) sits in functions with no FastAPI imports, unit-tested with a fake decide. llm.py is the LLM client. All inference goes through ctx.decide (background lane, one micro-batch at a time); no job kind is added, so the router does not depend on jobs.py. Routers publish through ClassifierStore.put(..., created_by="router:<name>").

LLM client (llm.py, httpx only, no SDK): 

class LLMError(RuntimeError): ...           # transport, HTTP status, timeout, schema-invalid response

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LLMResult:
    data: dict                              # the parsed JSON, already validated against the schema
    model: str
    input_tokens: int | None
    output_tokens: int | None
    latency_ms: float

class LLMClient(Protocol):
    async def complete_json(self, *, system: str, user: str, schema: dict, name: str,
                            max_tokens: int = 2048) -> LLMResult

class OpenAICompatClient:                   # POST {base_url}chat/completions, Authorization: Bearer <key>,
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, api_key: str, model: str, timeout_s: float = 60.0,
                 http: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> None
        # body: {"model", "messages": [system, user], "response_format": {"type": "json_schema",
        #        "json_schema": {"name", "schema", "strict": true}}, "max_tokens"}; 2 retries with backoff on
        #        429 / 5xx honouring Retry-After; if the content is not valid JSON, one tolerant parse (first
        #        JSON object in the text) before LLMError

def client_from_config(cfg: Config) -> LLMClient | None
    # None (router LLM off) unless CLEF_LLM_API_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY is set: in the process env, or in an env
    # file that dotenv.py loads before Config is built (./.env, ~/.config/clef/env; see the dotenv row of the
    # module table). Every call is logged to llm_calls.

Tables (created by C1 in 0002): 

CREATE TABLE routers (
    name           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,               -- NAME_RE
    owner          TEXT,
    classifier     TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,           -- the saved classifier it publishes to
    config         TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- JSON: instructions, domain_hint, gate, max_labels
    mode           TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- "review" | "auto"
    active_version INTEGER,                        -- NULL while cold (fewer than 1 real label)
    created_at     DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    updated_at     DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE router_label_sets (
    router             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES routers(name) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    version            INTEGER NOT NULL,
    labels             TEXT NOT NULL,              -- JSON {name: description}, including "other"
    source             TEXT NOT NULL,              -- "seed" | "bootstrap" | "proposal" | "manual" | "rollback"
    classifier_version INTEGER,                    -- the classifier version it was published as
    created_at         DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    created_by         TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (router, version)
);
CREATE TABLE review (
    id                 TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- "rev_" + 20 hex
    kind               TEXT NOT NULL,              -- "item" | "proposal"
    state              TEXT NOT NULL,              -- item: "open" | "buffered" | "resolved" | "discarded" |
                                                   --       "permanent_other" | "expired"
                                                   -- proposal: "open" | "accepted" | "rejected" | "failed"
    owner              TEXT,                       -- owner of the router / classifier
    router             TEXT,                       -- NULL for classifier low-confidence items
    classifier         TEXT,
    classifier_version INTEGER,
    reason             TEXT NOT NULL,              -- item: "other" | "low_confidence" | "ambiguous" | "cold";
                                                   -- proposal: "proposal" | "bootstrap"
    input              TEXT,                       -- JSON input; NULL once resolved or after CLEF_REVIEW_TTL_DAYS
    input_sha256       TEXT,                       -- of the canonical input (dedup, kept after the purge)
    prediction         TEXT,                       -- JSON {"label", "confidence", "scores"} at capture time
    proposal           TEXT,                       -- JSON (kind=proposal): {"labels": [{"name", "description",
                                                   --   "member_ids", "rationale", "nearest_existing"}], "stats"}
    label              TEXT,                       -- the human label (item) / accepted names (proposal, JSON)
    reroutes           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at         DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    resolved_at        DOUBLE PRECISION,
    resolved_by        TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX review_state ON review(state, created_at);
CREATE INDEX review_router ON review(router, state);
CREATE TABLE llm_calls (
    id            BIGINT PRIMARY KEY /* identity */,
    ts            DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    router        TEXT,
    purpose       TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- "propose" | "bootstrap"
    provider_url  TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- base URL (no key)
    model         TEXT NOT NULL,
    status        TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- "ok" | "error"
    latency_ms    DOUBLE PRECISION,
    input_tokens  BIGINT,
    output_tokens BIGINT,
    items         INTEGER,
    error         TEXT
);

Trigger (per routed item, under the active label set with n options including other): - other wins → reason other, buffered. - top probability < τ(n) → reason low_confidence, buffered. τ(n) rises with the label count: 0.5 for n <= 10, 0.7 for 11-30, 0.85 for 31-64 (defaults; tuned on tickets_labelled.csv, per-router override config.gate.thresholds = [[10, 0.5], [30, 0.7], [64, 0.85]]). - top two within config.gate.margin (default 0.15) → reason ambiguous, review item, not buffered. - "Buffered" = a review row kind=item, state=buffered with the input stored (D17). The other label's description names the other labels in negative form up to 15 labels, then a generic sentence.

Buffering and calls: a flush happens when a router has CLEF_ROUTER_BATCH (20) buffered items, when the oldest buffered item is CLEF_ROUTER_FLUSH_S old, or on POST .../propose. One call in flight per router and one globally. The prompt carries the current labels and the buffered inputs truncated to CLEF_ROUTER_MAX_INPUT_CHARS, numbered (members are returned as indices, never as copied text), and asks for at most min(3, capacity) new labels. Capacity = min(config.max_labels, CLEF_MAX_LABELS - 1) real labels; at the cap no call is made. Response schema: {"proposals": [{"name", "description", "member_indices", "nearest_existing", "duplicate_of", "rationale"}], "covered_by": [{"index", "label"}], "unclear_indices": [int]} (strict; name matches NAME_RE, description <= 15 words).

Acceptance test (before a proposal is shown or activated): build the candidate set (current + proposal + other), re-classify the proposal's members with ctx.decide; it passes when at least max(2, 50%) land on the new label with p >= τ(n'). It fails as a duplicate when most land on one existing label. Human labels feed it: a member a human already labelled with an existing label counts against the proposal, and resolving an item with a label re-classifies its text under the active set before the text is purged, recording agreement in the item's prediction.recheck.

Review mode: passing proposals become review rows kind=proposal, state=open with the acceptance numbers. Auto mode: a passing proposal is activated at once, at most CLEF_ROUTER_MAX_NEW_PER_DAY labels per UTC day (beyond that it waits as a review row). Activation = new router_label_sets version → ClassifierStore.put → re-route the buffered items in the background; an item that still fails the gate gets reroutes += 1, and after 2 it becomes permanent_other (out of future batches; its input is set to NULL in the same statement, D17, since nothing reads it again; input_sha256 and the prediction stay).

Cold start: a router with no seeds has no label set (clef needs >= 2 options). Every routed item is answered other with reason cold without a forward, and buffered. At CLEF_ROUTER_COLD_BATCH (20) items one bootstrap call proposes 3-8 labels (maxItems 8); the result is one proposal row holding the whole starter set (approve all, or edit, at once). One seed is enough to start the normal loop ([seed, other]).

Low-confidence items from saved classifiers: ClassifierDef gains review_threshold: float | None (0..1, default None = off). On interactive single-label runs (POST /v1/classifiers/{name}[/batch], not jobs), a result with confidence < review_threshold creates a review row kind=item, reason=low_confidence, router=NULL with the input, in the classifier owner's queue. Only runs by the owner or an admin (auth off counts as admin) are captured: another key's run of the classifier is not captured at all, because storing it under the owner would hand that key's input text to the owner, and the caller cannot act on another owner's classifier review. A classifier with no owner (made while auth was off) is then captured only for admins. Media inputs are never captured.

Routes (scopes from Keys; owner-scoped like jobs, admins see all; OpenAPI models for every body):

Route Body / query Response PUT /v1/routers/{name} {"classifier"?: name (default = router name), "seeds"?: labels dict, "instructions"?, "domain_hint"?, "mode"?: "review"|"auto", "max_labels"?: 2..63, "gate"?: {"thresholds", "margin"}} the router: {"name", "owner", "classifier", "mode", "config", "active_version", "labels", "buffered", "open_reviews", "created_at", "updated_at"}. An existing single-label classifier's latest labels become the seeds when seeds is omitted; multi-label or score: 400; a classifier already owned by another router: 409 GET /v1/routers, GET /v1/routers/{name}, DELETE /v1/routers/{name} list / router / {"deleted"} (the classifier stays) POST /v1/routers/{name}/route {"input"} the classify response + {"router", "reason": "classified|other|low_confidence|ambiguous|cold", "label_set_version", "review_id"} POST /v1/routers/{name}/route/batch {"inputs": [...]} {"results": [...], "batch_ms", "request_id"} POST /v1/routers/{name}/propose 202 {"router", "items", "llm_call_id"}; 409 when a call is in flight; 503 router LLM is off (set GEMINI_API_KEY) GET /v1/routers/{name}/versions, POST /v1/routers/{name}/versions/{v}/activate versions newest first / the router (rollback publishes that version again as a new classifier version) GET /v1/review?kind&state&router&classifier&limit=50&offset=0 {"items": [<review row; input included while stored>], "total"} newest first GET /v1/review/{id} the review row POST /v1/review/{id}/resolve item: {"action": "label", "label"} or {"action": "discard"}; proposal: {"action": "approve", "labels"?: [{"name", "description"}] (edited subset)} or {"action": "reject"} the row; input set NULL for items

Errors: 400 (name, labels, capacity), 403 (scope / owner), 404, 409 (in-flight call, classifier taken, resolving a resolved row), 503 (LLM off for /propose; LLM failures are recorded in llm_calls and on the proposal, never surfaced on route).

Purge: every hour, review.input is set NULL for rows older than CLEF_REVIEW_TTL_DAYS (open / buffered items become expired). Resolved rows keep label, input_sha256 and prediction without text.

Console: one Review screen (static/screens/review.js): queue filters (kind, state, router, classifier), item cards (input, prediction, label picker, discard), proposal cards (labels, members, acceptance bars, approve / edit / reject), per-router panel (label set + versions with rollback, buffer size, mode, LLM status with an "external LLM: " badge, calls and tokens today).

Invariants: input text is stored only in review.input and only until resolved / TTL (D17); nothing leaves the machine unless an LLM key is set; the router never edits a classifier except by appending a version; single-label only (D8).

As built (E2; additions and deviations, nothing above changed in meaning): - Modules: besides router.py and llm.py, review.py holds ReviewStore (all SQL of review and llm_calls); router.py holds RouterStore (routers, router_label_sets), RouterService and the routes. No migration: everything was created in 0002. - LLMClient also exposes base_url and model. The response schema has no maxItems: the number of new labels (<= 3, <= 8 for the starter set, <= capacity), names, word limits and index bounds are enforced in code, and a violating proposal is dropped, not the call. Absent values are "" (strict-schema friendly), not null. client_from_config is called once in router(ctx) and stored in ctx.extra["llm_client"]; tests replace it. ctx.extra["review_capture"] is the hook the saved-classifier routes in main.py call. - config also holds CLEF_ROUTER_MODE. PUT /v1/routers/{name} takes seeds only on a new or cold router (400 otherwise: labels are only added). max_labels 2..63; capacity = min(max_labels, CLEF_MAX_LABELS - 1). - Router response gains classifier_version and llm: {"enabled", "host", "model", "calls_today", "input_tokens_today", "output_tokens_today", "errors_today"} (the console badge). POST .../propose runs the LLM call and the re-check before it answers 202 {"router", "items", "llm_call_id", "proposals", "queued", "activated"}; 502 when the LLM call failed (recorded in llm_calls), 400 at the label cap or with fewer than 2 buffered items. After a failed call the background loop skips that router for 5 minutes. - Review rows: items whose text is part of an open proposal are open (not buffered) until the proposal is resolved. Proposals the re-check refuses are stored with state="failed" and the acceptance numbers. reroutes counts every check an unplaced item has been through (a propose call that did not use it, a failed or rejected proposal, a re-route after publishing); at 2 the item is permanent_other. Items the LLM lists in covered_by or unclear_indices become open with prediction.llm_hint. Proposal label is a JSON list of the accepted names. - Background loop (every 15 s): flush due routers (batch full, or oldest item older than CLEF_ROUTER_FLUSH_S with

= 2 items, >= 5 for a cold start) and purge once an hour. A full batch also starts a flush right after the route call that completed it. The starter set of a cold router is exempt from CLEF_ROUTER_MAX_NEW_PER_DAY; its pruning keeps the labels that >= 2 buffered items land on and needs half of the items covered. - Human approval of an edited subset is not re-checked (a person decided); descriptions are 1-40 words there. - Scopes: as in Keys. Routers and review rows are owner-scoped (other owners get 404; PUT on another's router 403). - ClassifierDef.review_threshold is stored only when set. clef doctor reports whether the LLM is on. - Not built: tuning of the default thresholds on tickets_labelled.csv (needs the model; defaults are the contract's).

docs.title: Job scheduler
docs.text:
Module boundary: all in jobs.py (JobRunner + a Scheduler class). Kinds keep their validate / run signatures; scheduling happens per chunk inside decide_resilient, which every built-in kind (and evaluate, the batch kind) already uses. A custom kind that calls ctx.decide directly bypasses the scheduler; the contract is that kinds call job.decide(reqs) (= decide_resilient(ctx, job, reqs)).

Policy: - Classes, strict between classes: urgent (3) > high (2) > normal (1, default) > low (0). Aging: a waiting job's effective class rises one level per CLEF_JOB_AGING_S without a turn, never to urgent. - Fair share inside a class: stride scheduling per owner (principal name; NULL = one owner). pass += cost / weight, weight 1 for everyone in v3.2, cost = the chunk's records. The next turn goes to the lowest pass; an owner that comes back sets pass = max(own, current minimum). "Comes back" = goes from no runnable job to runnable: a new job, or a job leaving a pause (its window reopened, a slot came free); the minimum is over the owners that were runnable already (vtime when there are none), and an un-paused job's aging clock restarts, so a pause never banks turns. Within one owner: higher class first, then interrupted, then seq. State is in memory and rebuilt after a restart. - Turn gate: await scheduler.turn(job) before every engine call of a job; scheduler.done(job, cost) after. The gate wraps each engine call inside decide_resilient (so a bisected chunk takes one turn per call and no turn is held while a job waits for an unavailable engine). One job chunk in flight across all jobs (as today): interactive work still goes first through the engine's lanes. A unit test asserts the background lane never holds more than one job chunk. - Active set: up to CLEF_JOB_ACTIVE jobs are claimed (JobStore.claim(job_id), chosen in stride order) and run as their own asyncio tasks; all of them show running (D9). runner.current becomes a set; progress webhooks are per job. claim(job_id) returns the claimed row (plus claimed_from) or None; claim_next stays for tools and tests but the runner no longer uses it. An urgent job does not wait for a free slot (it is admitted at once, even above CLEF_JOB_ACTIVE), or the class would mean nothing while four normal jobs run. Candidates are ordered like turn waiters (class after aging, owner pass, jobs the owner already runs, interrupted, seq). - Fair slots: when no slot is free and a job of another owner waits for one (queued in its window, or running and paused active_limit), an owner holding more than its share (ceil(CLEF_JOB_ACTIVE / owners wanting slots), at least 1; urgent jobs hold no counted slot) gives up its youngest job (highest seq; among over-share owners, the one holding most). The victim finishes its chunk in flight, then stays running with waiting_reason: "active_limit" (D9: like a job paused off-hours, it keeps its task, its progress and its quota reservation; nothing is parked or re-claimed) and gets the next free slot. A job of a higher effective class than the waiter never yields, an urgent job never yields, and a waiter whose owner already holds its share takes nothing. A single owner with nobody waiting still uses every slot. A free slot goes first to the waiting job whose owner holds the fewest. So CLEF_JOB_ACTIVE bounds the jobs taking turns, not the job tasks. - Windows: schedule = {"window": "HH:MM-HH:MM", "tz": "<IANA>"} per job (default CLEF_JOB_WINDOW in CLEF_JOB_TZ). start > end crosses midnight; start == end = 24 h. Aware datetimes via zoneinfo; on DST days an edge inside the skipped hour starts at the next valid minute, the repeated hour uses fold=0; an instance whose two edges fall in the same skipped hour is empty that day, and next_start skips it (it returns only a moment contains accepts). A job gets turns only inside its window. A queued job outside it stays queued; a running job that leaves it stays running but gets no turns and frees its active slot. Both show waiting_reason: "off_hours" and next_window_at. Unknown tz or a bad window: 400 at submit. - urgent: true needs the urgent scope (403 otherwise), sets class urgent and ignores the window. - Expiry: expire_after_s counts from eligible_at (the first moment the job could take a turn, i.e. when its window first opens; D19). An expired job stops between chunks and ends cancelled with error = "expired" (no new status; JobInfo.expired: true). - Quota at submit, in this order: idempotency lookup (a replay returns the existing job and is not charged) → validate / snapshot → ctx.quotas.reserve(principal, total) (in memory; 429 when it does not fit) → JobStore.create(..., quota_day, quota_reserved). If create raises (JobsFull, an idempotency race that returns another job, a DB error), the reservation is refunded in full before the error is returned. The whole job is charged to the submit day; on cancelled / failed / expiry, total - done is refunded to that day. Env principals and auth off: no reservation. Cache hits are not charged (D23 #3): each chunk's hits (Prepared.hits from ctx.prepare) are handed back to the reservation once the chunk's rows are stored, and quota_reserved drops by the same number in that transaction, which also adds them to jobs.hits (migration 0003). Credited hits are capped at what is still reserved, and exactly the credited number goes back to the quota. The final refund of a cancelled / failed job is quota_reserved - done + hits, read from the row, so it is exact after a restart too; a non-resumable job that restarts from 0 resets hits with its rows.

Python API (for E2-free kinds and F1, so they never edit jobs.py): 

class JobRunner:
    async def submit(self, kind: str, payload: dict, *, principal: Principal | None, metadata: dict | None = None,
                     webhook: dict | None = None, priority: str = "normal", urgent: bool = False,
                     schedule: dict | None = None, expire_after_s: float | None = None,
                     idem_key: str | None = None) -> dict
        # validation, snapshot, model check, quota reservation, create, poke; raises ValueError (400),
        # PermissionError (403, urgent), QuotaExceeded (429), JobsFull (409), LookupError (404, unknown
        # model). POST /v1/jobs uses it (through `submit_ex`, which also says whether the job was a replay).
    async def cancel(self, job_id: str) -> dict
    def get(self, job_id: str) -> dict | None
class JobHandle:
    async def decide(self, reqs: list[SystemOneRequest]) -> list[Any]   # turn gate + decide_resilient
    async def add_items(self, items: list[dict], tokens: int = 0) -> None  # tokens -> jobs.tokens
Kind spec keys (added): "completed_if_all_failed": bool (default False; True = a run where every item failed still ends succeeded, as OpenAI batches do). Existing keys unchanged.

HTTP: POST /v1/jobs gains priority (low|normal|high), urgent (bool), schedule, expire_after_s. JobInfo gains priority, urgent, schedule, waiting_reason (null | "off_hours" | "active_limit" | "turn"), next_window_at (ISO or null), expired, model, tokens. GET /v1/jobs gains ?priority=. Statuses are unchanged.

Env: CLEF_JOB_TZ, CLEF_JOB_WINDOW, CLEF_JOB_ACTIVE, CLEF_JOB_AGING_S. New dep tzdata in the server extra. Tables: the E1 jobs columns in Storage.

Errors: 400 bad window / tz / priority; 403 urgent without the scope; 409 CLEF_MAX_JOBS; 429 quota.

Invariants: one job chunk in flight; rows stay contiguous 0..done-1 (F2's length sort persists each window in input order); recover() unchanged; webhooks unchanged.

docs.title: Job throughput: window sort and tokenize ahead (F2, jobsort.py)
docs.text: Opt-in, both default off (CLEF_JOB_SORT_WINDOW, CLEF_TOKENIZE_AHEAD), benchmark-gated (bench/sort_check.sh). run_chunked and the evaluate kind build a jobsort.windowed(ctx, n, build, decide_resilient) once per run; it is None with both flags off, and then the original loop runs unchanged. - A step is one window: CLEF_JOB_SORT_WINDOW items (never fewer than CLEF_MAX_MICROBATCH), or one micro-batch when only tokenizing ahead. The caller builds the window's requests and calls sorter.decide(job, start, reqs), which returns results in the same order as reqs. - decide encodes the whole window with ctx.prepare (CPU threads), orders the records that need a forward (no cache hit, no in-window duplicate) by (is_media, token length), stable, and queues them with ctx.decide_prepared(priority="background") in micro-batches of CLEF_MAX_MICROBATCH: one micro-batch in flight, as before; interactive work still goes first through the engine lanes. Hits and duplicates are put back as Engine.submit would (timing.cached). - Persistence: the caller persists the whole window in one add_items in input order. Rows stay contiguous 0..done-1; a crash, clean stop or cancel inside a window leaves done at the window start (at most one window is recomputed on resume; the resume point need not be window aligned). Progress and the circuit breaker advance once per window. - Tokenize ahead: after window k is encoded, a task encodes window k+1 while k is on the GPU. One GPU worker only. The prefetch looks the cache up before window k's results are stored, so a duplicate in the next window is computed again (same row content, only cache statistics differ). - Errors: a failed prefetch or encode, or a micro-batch the engine rejects (ValueError, OOM, not ready), is re-run through decide_resilient for just those records, so isolation, bisection and the engine wait behave as without the flags. Cancel is checked between micro-batches. - Scheduler: each micro-batch takes a turn (JobHandle.engine_prepared, the gated hand-off) and the window's cache hits are noted on the handle (not charged); the fallback goes through decide_resilient, also gated.

docs.title: OpenAI Files and Batches
docs.text:
Module boundary: batches.py is a feature module listed in FEATURES before jobs (it registers the batch job kind); it reaches the runner lazily through ctx.extra["jobs"] and only through the JobRunner / JobHandle API (Job scheduler). compat_openai.py is split into pure prepare_chat(body: dict, cfg) -> ChatPlan (raises SchemaError) and render_chat(plan, result, request_id) -> dict; the live route and the batch kind both use them. Errors on these routes use the OpenAI shape (route_class(ctx, openai_error)). New dep python-multipart in the server extra.

Tables (created by C1 in 0002): 

CREATE TABLE files (
    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                  -- "file-" + 24 hex
    owner      TEXT,
    purpose    TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- "batch" (uploads) | "batch_output" (generated)
    role       TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- "input" | "output" | "error"
    filename   TEXT NOT NULL,
    bytes      BIGINT NOT NULL,                   -- input: on disk; output/error: computed when the job ends
    lines      INTEGER,
    job_id     TEXT REFERENCES jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,   -- output/error files only
    created_at DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    expires_at DOUBLE PRECISION
);
CREATE INDEX files_owner ON files(owner, created_at);
CREATE TABLE batches (
    id                TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- "batch_" + the job id's 20 hex
    job_id            TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES jobs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    owner             TEXT,
    endpoint          TEXT NOT NULL,              -- "/v1/chat/completions" | "/v1/classify" | "/v1/score"
    input_file_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    output_file_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
    error_file_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    completion_window TEXT NOT NULL,              -- "24h"
    metadata          TEXT,
    errors            TEXT,                       -- JSON list of {code, line, message, param} (status failed)
    created_at        DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    cancelling_at     DOUBLE PRECISION
);
Input content lives on disk at <state_dir>/files/<id>.jsonl (path built only from a validated id, streamed to a temp file with the size cap, then renamed). Output and error files are virtual: their content is streamed from the job's rows. They live as long as the job (CLEF_JOB_TTL_HOURS); input files until expires_at (expires_after or CLEF_FILE_TTL_HOURS).

Routes (scope jobs; owner-scoped, admins see all; integer unix-second timestamps):

Route Request Response POST /v1/files multipart: file (.jsonl), purpose=batch, optional expires_after[anchor]=created_at, expires_after[seconds] (3600..2592000) FileObject GET /v1/files?after&limit=20&order=desc&purpose {"object": "list", "data": [FileObject], "first_id", "last_id", "has_more"} GET /v1/files/{id} FileObject DELETE /v1/files/{id} {"id", "object": "file", "deleted": true}; output / error files: 400 (delete the batch's job instead) GET /v1/files/{id}/content the JSONL bytes, application/jsonl, streamed POST /v1/batches {"input_file_id", "endpoint", "completion_window": "24h", "metadata"?, "clef"?: {"priority", "urgent", "schedule"}} Batch GET /v1/batches/{id} Batch GET /v1/batches?after&limit=20 limit 1..100, newest first cursor list as for files POST /v1/batches/{id}/cancel Batch (cancelling or cancelled)

FileObject: {"id", "object": "file", "bytes", "created_at", "expires_at", "filename", "purpose", "status": "processed", "status_details": null}.

Batch: {"id", "object": "batch", "endpoint", "errors", "input_file_id", "completion_window", "status", "output_file_id", "error_file_id", "created_at", "in_progress_at", "expires_at", "finalizing_at", "completed_at", "failed_at", "expired_at", "cancelling_at", "cancelled_at", "request_counts": {"total", "completed", "failed"}, "metadata", "model", "usage": {"input_tokens", "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 0, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens"}}. request_counts.completed = done - failed; usage.input_tokens = jobs.tokens; model = spec.id; expires_at = eligible_at + 24h (always set: the scheduler sets eligible_at at submit, to the next time the window opens). The SDK's extra_body={"clef": {...}} lands as the top-level clef field.

Mapping to jobs (one batch = one job of kind batch, visible in GET /v1/jobs?kind=batch; submitted through JobRunner.submit(..., expire_after_s=86400); the batch kind spec itself sets "completed_if_all_failed": True): - Create validates at submit, in the threadpool: the file exists, belongs to the caller and has purpose=batch; every line is JSON with a unique custom_id, method == "POST" and url == endpoint; at most min(CLEF_MAX_BATCH_LINES, CLEF_MAX_JOB_ITEMS) lines. A structural failure creates the batch with status failed and errors.data = [{code, line, message, param}] (no job runs), as OpenAI does. A body that fails translation (prepare_chat / classify / score validation) becomes an error-file line, not a batch failure. endpoint outside the three: 400 param: "endpoint". stream: true in a body: an error line.

Job state Batch status validation failed (no job) failed queued, running, interrupted in_progress (cancelling once a cancel was requested) succeeded completed failed (systemic) failed, errors.data = [{"code": "server_error", "message"}]; rows so far are still served cancelled, error = "expired" expired cancelled cancelled

Rows: {"index", "custom_id", "status_code", "body" | "error", "input_tokens"}. Output file line = {"id": "batch_req_<20hex>_<index>", "custom_id", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id", "body"}, "error": null} for 2xx rows; the error file streams the non-2xx rows (OpenAI error body) plus, for a finished job, {"response": null, "error": {"code": "batch_expired" | "batch_cancelled", "message"}} for every input line with no row (custom ids re-read from the input file). Output order is input order.

Limits: CLEF_MAX_FILE_MB (body limit of POST /v1/files only, applied in GuardMiddleware), CLEF_MAX_BATCH_LINES, CLEF_FILE_TTL_HOURS; metadata <= 16 pairs, keys <= 64 chars, values <= 512 chars; completion_window must be "24h". Rate limit (ctx.limited) on POST /v1/files and POST /v1/batches. Quota: the batch reserves its line count at create (Job scheduler).

Errors (OpenAI shape): 400 invalid_request_error (bad purpose, endpoint, window, metadata, file not .jsonl), 403, 404 (unknown or foreign file / batch), 409 (CLEF_MAX_JOBS), 413 (file too large), 429 (rate_limit_exceeded / insufficient_quota).

Invariants: files are never in the DB; virtual files never exist on disk; deleting a batch's job deletes its batch and output / error file rows; the batch path uses the same translation as the live routes, so probabilities match /v1/chat/completions.

As built (F1; clarifications and deviations from the text above, nothing else changed): - prepare_chat(body, cfg, model) takes the served model id the caller already resolved (served_model; its UnknownModel is the route's 404, a model_not_found line in a batch). render_chat(chat, result, request_id, total_ms=None) returns the non-streaming body; chat_outcome returns the parts the streaming route also needs. - jobs.py was touched in three places the contract did not list: JobStore.add_items sums the rows' input_tokens into jobs.tokens (an explicit tokens= count wins); the circuit breaker ignores rows that carry a 4xx status_code (a bad batch line is the client's mistake, still counted in jobs.failed); _execute honours completed_if_all_failed. Each exists once, in jobs.py. - Defaults: CLEF_MAX_FILE_MB 200 (OpenAI's limit), CLEF_MAX_BATCH_LINES 50000, CLEF_FILE_TTL_HOURS 720. - A structurally failed batch still needs the batches.job_id foreign key, so it gets a terminal failed job row (kind batch, payload {}, nothing reserved, never runnable) written in the same transaction as the batch. - output_file_id / error_file_id are null until usable: the batch ended, and the output file has a success / the error file a failed or never-run line. A batch that failed validation has neither. - Clarification: an input file that an unfinished batch references cannot be deleted (409) and is skipped by the TTL purge, because the error file re-reads the custom ids from it. After the batch ended the input file may go; the error file then omits the lines that never ran. - Clarification: admins list, read and delete every file and batch, but POST /v1/batches only accepts an input file the caller uploaded (404 otherwise). The batch job re-checks that the file's owner is the job's owner when it runs, so POST /v1/jobs {"kind": "batch"} cannot read another key's file. The job's quota reservation is the file row's lines, never the payload's. - A line nested too deeply for the JSON parser (RecursionError) is an invalid_json_line like any other bad JSON (and an error row if it is met at run time), never a 500. - POST /v1/jobs {"kind": "batch"} gets the same structural scan at submit, through the kind's snapshot hook (submit only, not on every run or resume): a structural problem is a 400 naming the first bad line. It scans only a file owned by the submitter (jobs.SUBMIT_OWNER), so it never describes another key's file; POST /v1/batches marks the file it scanned itself (a context variable), so a batch is not scanned twice. - The seam to the scheduler is batches.submit_batch_job, a call to JobRunner.submit with the caller's principal, clef.priority, clef.urgent, clef.schedule and expire_after_s = 86400. It maps ValueError to 400 (a bad option), PermissionError to 403 (urgent without the scope), a model not served to 404, JobsFull to 409 and QuotaExceeded to 429. The scheduler reserves the quota once, at submit, from the input file's stored line count, and sets eligible_at (the submit time, or the next time the window opens), so the batch's expires_at is known from the start: eligible_at + 24h. - The audit actions are batch.cancel and file.delete, as listed in Storage.
